translations.literal: Han Mao; Pi Baozi; Feng Chiwen; Lu Luohan; Kong Bogong; Tian Yizong; Meng Biao; Xi Kangsheng; Yang Dayan; Cui Yanbo; Li Shuren
translations.idiomatic: Han Mao, Pi Baozi, Feng Chiwen, Lu Luohan, Kong Bogong, Tian Yizong, Meng Biao, Xi Kangsheng, Yang Dayan, Cui Yanbo, and Li Shuren

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十五

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Twenty-Five
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 25

sentences.zh: 韓茂皮豹子封敕文呂羅漢孔伯恭田益宗孟表奚康生楊大眼崔延伯李叔仁

translations.literal: Han Mao, Pi Baozi, Feng Chiwen, Lu Luohan, Kong Bogong, Tian Yizong, Meng Biao, Xi Kangsheng, Yang Dayan, Cui Yanbo, Li Shuren
translations.idiomatic: Han Mao, Pi Baozi, Feng Chiwen, Lu Luohan, Kong Bogong, Tian Yizong, Meng Biao, Xi Kangsheng, Yang Dayan, Cui Yanbo, and Li Shuren

sentences.zh: 韓茂，字元興，安定安武人也。

translations.literal: Han Mao, styled Yuanying, was a man of Anwu in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Han Mao, styled Yuanying, was from Anwu in Anding.

sentences.zh: 父耆字黃耇，永興中，自赫連屈丐來降，位常山太守，假安武侯，仍居常山之九門。

translations.literal: His father Qi, styled Huanggao, in the Yongxing era came down from Helian Quchu to submit; he held the post of Inspector of Changshan, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anwu in name, and still resided at Jiumen in Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qi, styled Huanggao, submitted from Helian Quchu's domain in the Yongxing era, served as Inspector of Changshan, was enfeoffed in name as Marquis of Anwu, and continued to live at Jiumen in Changshan.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈涇州刺史，諡曰成。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously made Inspector of Jingzhou, with the posthumous title Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously appointed Inspector of Jingzhou and given the posthumous title Cheng.

sentences.zh: 茂年十七，膂力過人，尤善騎射。

translations.literal: At seventeen Mao's physical strength surpassed others, and he was especially skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen, Mao's strength surpassed that of ordinary men, and he was especially skilled in mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 明元曾親征丁零翟猛，茂為中軍執幢。

translations.literal: Emperor Mingyuan once personally campaigned against the Dingling Zhai Meng; Mao served in the central army holding the standard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingyuan personally led a campaign against the Dingling chieftain Zhai Meng, Mao served in the central army as bearer of the command standard.

sentences.zh: 時大風，諸軍旌旗皆偃僕，茂於馬上持幢，初不傾倒。

translations.literal: At that time a great wind blew and the banners of all the armies were blown flat; Mao on horseback held the standard and it did not tilt at first.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce wind arose, and the banners of every army were blown flat; yet Mao, mounted, held his standard upright without the slightest waver.

sentences.zh: 帝異而問之，謂左右曰：「記之。

translations.literal: The emperor found it strange and questioned him, saying to those beside him, "Record this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was astonished and questioned him, then said to his attendants, "Make a record of this.

sentences.zh: 」尋征詣行在所，以為武賁郎將。

translations.literal: " Soon he was summoned to the mobile court and made a Martial Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: " He was soon summoned to the emperor's camp and appointed Martial Guard General.

sentences.zh: 後從太武討赫連昌，大破之，以功賜爵蒲陰子，遷侍輦郎。

translations.literal: Later he followed Emperor Taiwu in attacking Helian Chang, inflicted a great defeat, and for his merit was granted the title of Baron of Puyin; he was transferred to Attendant of the Imperial Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He later followed Emperor Taiwu against Helian Chang, won a great victory, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Puyin for his merit; he was then promoted to Attendant of the Imperial Carriage.

sentences.zh: 又從破統萬，平平涼，當茂所沖，莫不應弦而殪。

translations.literal: Again he followed in the capture of Tongwan and the pacification of Liangzhou; wherever Mao charged, none failed to fall to his bowstring.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed the campaigns that took Tongwan and pacified Liangzhou; wherever Mao led the charge, the enemy fell to his bow without exception.

sentences.zh: 拜內侍長，進爵九門侯。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of Palace Attendants and advanced to Marquis of Jiumen.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of Palace Attendants and advanced to Marquis of Jiumen.

sentences.zh: 後從征蠕蠕，頻戰大捷。

translations.literal: Later he followed campaigns against the Rouran and repeatedly won great victories.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined campaigns against the Rouran and won repeated great victories.

sentences.zh: 與樂平王丕等伐和龍，茂為前鋒都將，戰功居多。

translations.literal: With Prince of Le Ping and others he attacked Helong; Mao was vanguard commander and his battle achievements were the greater part.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Helong with the Prince of Le Ping and others, Mao served as vanguard commander and accounted for most of the victories.

sentences.zh: 遷司衛監，錄前後功，拜散騎常侍、殿中尚書，進爵安定公。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of Palace Guards; his earlier and later merits were recorded, and he was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Palace Secretariat, advancing to Duke of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director of Palace Guards; his past and recent achievements were entered on record, and he was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Palace Secretariat, advancing to Duke of Anding.

sentences.zh: 從破薛永宗、蓋吳，轉都官尚書。

translations.literal: He followed in the defeat of Xue Yongzong and Gai Wu and was transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing for Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the campaigns that defeated Xue Yongzong and Gai Wu and was transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing for Personnel.

sentences.zh: 從車駕南征，拜徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He followed the imperial carriage on the southern expedition and was appointed Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor on the southern expedition and was appointed Inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 還，拜侍中、尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Attendant-in-Chief and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Attendant-in-Chief and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 文成踐阼，拜尚書令，加侍中、征南大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wencheng ascended the throne, Mao was appointed Director of the Masters of Writing, with the additional titles of Attendant-in-Chief and General Who Conquers the South.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wencheng took the throne, Mao was appointed Director of the Masters of Writing and additionally made Attendant-in-Chief and General Who Conquers the South.

sentences.zh: 茂沈毅篤實，雖無文學，每議論合理，為將善於撫眾，勇冠當世，為朝廷所稱。

translations.literal: Mao was deep, resolute, and sincere; though without literary learning, whenever he spoke in council his reasoning was sound; as a general he was good at comforting the troops, and his courage was foremost in his age—he was praised by the court.
translations.idiomatic: Mao was grave, steadfast, and sincere; though he had no literary training, his counsel in council was always sound. As a general he excelled at winning the loyalty of his men, and his courage was unmatched in his generation—the court spoke highly of him.

sentences.zh: 太安二年，領太子少師。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tai'an he was made Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Tai'an era he was appointed Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈涇州刺史，安定王，諡曰桓。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made Inspector of Jingzhou and Prince of Anding, with the posthumous title Huan.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously appointed Inspector of Jingzhou and Prince of Anding, with the posthumous title Huan.

sentences.zh: 長子備，字延德，賜爵行唐侯，曆太子庶子、甯西將軍，典游獵曹，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His eldest son Bei, styled Yande, was granted the title Marquis of Xingtang; he successively held the posts of Household Companion to the Heir Apparent and General Who Guards the West, and directed the Bureau of Imperial Hunts, with the additional title of Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Bei, styled Yande, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xingtang, served successively as Household Companion to the Heir Apparent and General Who Guards the West, directed the Bureau of Imperial Hunts, and was given the additional title of Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 襲爵安定公、征南大將軍。

translations.literal: He inherited the title Duke of Anding and the post General Who Conquers the South.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title Duke of Anding and the post of General Who Conquers the South.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈雍州刺史。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously appointed Inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 諡曰簡。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously known as Jian.

sentences.zh: 備弟均，字天德，少善射，有將略。

translations.literal: Bei's younger brother Jun, styled Tiande, was skilled at archery from youth and had military talent.
translations.idiomatic: Bei's younger brother Jun, styled Tiande, was an expert archer from youth and possessed real military talent.

sentences.zh: 初為中散，賜爵范陽子，遷金部尚書，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At first he was a Central Attendant; he was granted the title Baron of Fanyang and transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing for Revenue, with the additional title of Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a Central Attendant, was enfeoffed as Baron of Fanyang, and was transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing for Revenue with the additional title of Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 兄備卒，無子，均襲爵安定公、征南大將軍。

translations.literal: When his elder brother Bei died without a son, Jun inherited the title Duke of Anding and the post General Who Conquers the South.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder brother Bei died without an heir, Jun inherited the title Duke of Anding and the post of General Who Conquers the South.

sentences.zh: 曆定、青、冀三州刺史，甚有譽。

translations.literal: He successively held the three inspectorates of Ding, Qing, and Ji and won high reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as inspector of Ding, Qing, and Ji provinces and earned a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 廣阿澤在定、冀、相三州界，土曠人稀，多有寇盜，乃置鎮以靜之。

translations.literal: The Guang'a Marsh lay on the border of Ding, Ji, and Xiang provinces; the land was broad and the people sparse, and bandits were numerous, so a garrison was established to pacify the region.
translations.idiomatic: Guang'a Marsh lay where Ding, Ji, and Xiang provinces met; the land was open and sparsely settled, and banditry was common, so the court established a garrison to keep the area quiet.

sentences.zh: 以均在冀州，劫盜止息，除大將軍、廣阿鎮大將，加都督三州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Because Jun was in Jizhou, robbery and plunder ceased; he was made a Grand General and Grand General of the Guang'a Garrison, with the added authority of Commander over the military affairs of the three provinces.
translations.idiomatic: With Jun stationed in Jizhou, highway robbery ceased. He was appointed Grand General and Grand General of the Guang'a Garrison, with added authority as commander over military affairs in all three provinces.

sentences.zh: 均清身率下，禁斷奸邪，於是趙郡屠各、西山丁零聚黨山澤以劫害為業者，均皆誘慰追捕，遠近震跼。

translations.literal: Jun led by personal integrity and restrained his subordinates, forbidding wickedness; thus the Tujue of Zhao commandery, the Dingling of the western hills, and others who had gathered in the mountains and marshes to live by plunder were all enticed, reassured, and pursued—near and far were shaken into submission.
translations.idiomatic: Jun led by personal integrity, kept his men in order, and cracked down on crime. The Tujue of Zhao commandery, the Dingling of the western hills, and others who had banded together in mountain and marsh country to live by robbery were enticed back, reassured, or hunted down, and both near and far were cowed into submission.

sentences.zh: 先是，河外未賓，人多去就，故權立東青州，為招懷之本。

translations.literal: Before this, the lands beyond the Yellow River had not yet submitted; many people went back and forth, so the Eastern Qingzhou was set up provisionally as a base for winning them over.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the country south of the Yellow River had not yet submitted, and people moved freely between the two sides; the court therefore established Eastern Qingzhou as a provisional base for winning them over.

sentences.zh: 新附人咸受優復，然舊人奸逃者，多往投焉。

translations.literal: The newly submitted all received favorable exemptions, yet many of the old subjects who had fled to crime went over to join them.
translations.idiomatic: Newly submitted households all received favorable tax exemptions, yet many older subjects who had turned to banditry went over to join them.

sentences.zh: 均表陳非便，朝議罷之。

translations.literal: Jun memorialized that this was not advantageous; the court debated and abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: Jun submitted a memorial arguing that the arrangement was harmful; after deliberation the court abolished Eastern Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 後均所統，劫盜頗起，獻文詔書讓之。

translations.literal: Later in the territory Jun governed, banditry arose again in considerable numbers, and Emperor Xianwen issued an edict reproaching him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, under Jun's jurisdiction, banditry flared up again on a considerable scale, and Emperor Xianwen sent an edict reproaching him.

sentences.zh: 又以五州人戶殷多，編籍不實，詔均檢括，出十餘萬戶。

translations.literal: Also, because the households of the five provinces were numerous and the registers were inaccurate, an edict ordered Jun to examine and correct them, turning up more than a hundred thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Because the five provinces had large populations but inaccurate household registers, the court ordered Jun to audit them and uncovered more than a hundred thousand unregistered households.

sentences.zh: 復授定州刺史，百姓安之。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Inspector of Dingzhou, and the people lived in peace under him.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed Inspector of Dingzhou, and the people lived securely under his rule.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 諡康公。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Duke Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously known as Duke Kang.

sentences.zh: 皮豹子，漁陽人也。

translations.literal: Pi Baozi was a man of Yuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Pi Baozi was from Yuyang.

sentences.zh: 少有武略。

translations.literal: In youth he had martial talent.
translations.idiomatic: Even in youth he showed martial ability.

sentences.zh: 泰常中，為中散。

translations.literal: In the Taichang era he was a Central Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taichang era he served as a Central Attendant.

sentences.zh: 太武時，為散騎常侍，賜爵新安侯，又拜選部尚書。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Taiwu he was Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, granted the title Marquis of Xin'an, and also appointed Director of the Masters of Writing for Selection.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taiwu he was Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, enfeoffed as Marquis of Xin'an, and also appointed Director of the Masters of Writing for Selection.

sentences.zh: 後除開府儀同三司，進爵淮陽公，鎮長安，坐盜官財，徙于統萬。

translations.literal: Later he was made Bearer of the Staff with the Same Powers as the Three Excellencies, advanced to Duke of Huaiyang, and stationed at Chang'an; he was demoted to Tongwan for embezzling official property.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Bearer of the Staff with the Same Powers as the Three Excellencies, advanced to Duke of Huaiyang, and stationed at Chang'an, but was banished to Tongwan for embezzling government property.

sentences.zh: 真君三年，宋將裴方明等侵南秦王楊難當，遂陷仇池。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenjun, the Song generals Pei Fangming and others invaded the Southern Qin king Yang Nan'dang and then took Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenjun, Song generals led by Pei Fangming invaded the Southern Qin king Yang Nan'dang and then captured Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 太武征豹子，復其爵位，尋拜使持節、仇池鎮將，督並中諸軍與建興公古弼等分命諸將，十道並進。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu summoned Baozi and restored his title and post; soon he was appointed Commissioner with the Staff, Garrison Commander of Chouchi, supervising the armies of Bing and Zhong provinces together with the Duke of Jianxing, Gu Bibi, and others, who were each assigned commands—the ten routes advanced together.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu recalled Baozi and restored his rank and office; he was soon appointed Commissioner with the Staff and Garrison Commander of Chouchi, placed in overall command of the armies of Bing and Zhong provinces together with the Duke of Jianxing, Gu Bibi, and others, with the various commanders advancing along ten routes at once.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，豹子進擊樂鄉，大破之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, Baozi advanced and attacked Leyang, inflicting a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year, Baozi advanced against Leyang and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 宋使其秦州刺史胡崇之鎮仇池，至漢中，聞官軍已西，懼不敢進。

translations.literal: The Song appointed Hu Chongzhi Inspector of Qinzhou to garrison Chouchi; when he reached Hanzhong and heard that the government army had already marched west, he was afraid and did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: The Song appointed Hu Chongzhi Inspector of Qinzhou to hold Chouchi; when he reached Hanzhong and learned that the imperial army had already marched west, fear kept him from advancing.

sentences.zh: 豹子與司馬楚之至濁水，擊禽崇之，盡虜其眾。

translations.literal: Baozi with Sima Chu reached Zhuoshui, attacked and captured Chongzhi, and took all his troops captive.
translations.idiomatic: Baozi and Sima Chu reached Zhuoshui, attacked and captured Chongzhi, and took his entire force prisoner.

sentences.zh: 仇池平。

translations.literal: Chouchi was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Chouchi was pacified.

sentences.zh: 未幾，諸氐復推楊文德為主以圍仇池，古弼討平之。

translations.literal: Before long the various Di again set up Yang Wende as leader to besiege Chouchi; Gu Bibi campaigned and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Di clans again raised Yang Wende as their leader and besieged Chouchi; Gu Bibi campaigned against them and restored order.

sentences.zh: 時豹子次下辨，聞圍解，欲還。

translations.literal: At that time Baozi was encamped at Xia Bian; hearing that the siege was lifted, he wished to return.
translations.idiomatic: Baozi was then encamped at Xia Bian; when he heard the siege had been raised, he wished to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 弼使謂豹子曰：「賊恥其負敗，必求報復，不如陳兵以待之。

translations.literal: Bi sent word to Baozi saying, "The enemy, shamed by defeat, will surely seek revenge; better to array your troops and wait for them.
translations.idiomatic: Bi sent word to Baozi: "The enemy, shamed by defeat, will surely seek revenge. It would be better to hold your army in readiness and wait.

sentences.zh: 」豹子以為然。

translations.literal: " Baozi thought this right.
translations.idiomatic: " Baozi agreed.

sentences.zh: 尋除都督秦、雍、荊、梁、益五州諸軍事，進號征西大將軍、開府，仇池鎮將、持節、公如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Commander over the military affairs of Qin, Yong, Jing, Liang, and Yi provinces, advanced to General Who Conquers the West and Bearer of the Staff, retaining his posts as Garrison Commander of Chouchi, Commissioner with the Staff, and Duke as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed commander over military affairs in Qin, Yong, Jing, Liang, and Yi provinces, advanced to General Who Conquers the West and Bearer of the Staff, while retaining his posts as Garrison Commander of Chouchi, Commissioner with the Staff, and duke as before.

sentences.zh: 宋復遣楊文德、姜道盛寇濁水，別遣將青陽顯伯守斧山，以拒豹子。

translations.literal: The Song again sent Yang Wende and Jiang Daosheng to raid Zhuoshui, and separately sent the general Qingyang Xianbo to hold Fushan to block Baozi.
translations.idiomatic: The Song again sent Yang Wende and Jiang Daosheng to raid Zhuoshui and separately dispatched the general Qingyang Xianbo to hold Fushan and block Baozi.

sentences.zh: 濁水城兵射殺道盛。

translations.literal: The troops of Zhuoshui city shot and killed Daosheng.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison at Zhuoshui shot and killed Daosheng.

sentences.zh: 豹子至斧山，斬顯伯，悉俘其眾。

translations.literal: Baozi reached Fushan, beheaded Xianbo, and took all his troops captive.
translations.idiomatic: Baozi reached Fushan, beheaded Xianbo, and took his entire force prisoner.

sentences.zh: 初，南秦王楊難當歸命，詔送楊氏子弟詣京師。

translations.literal: At first the Southern Qin king Yang Nan'dang had submitted; an edict ordered the Yang clansmen sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Southern Qin king Yang Nan'dang had submitted to the court, and an edict ordered Yang clansmen sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 文德以行賂得留，出奔漢中。

translations.literal: Wende, by bribery, was allowed to remain; he fled to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wende bribed his way into being allowed to stay behind and fled to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 宋以文德為武都王，守葭蘆城，招誘氐羌。

translations.literal: The Song made Wende Prince of Wudu and had him guard the Jialu fortress, to entice the Di and Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Song made Wende Prince of Wudu, stationed him at Jialu fortress, and used him to win over the Di and Qiang.

sentences.zh: 於是武都陰平五部氐人叛應文德，詔豹子討之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Di of the five divisions of Wudu and Yinping rebelled and answered Wende; an edict ordered Baozi to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: The Di of the five divisions of Wudu and Yinping then rose in rebellion and rallied to Wende; an edict ordered Baozi to campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 文德阻兵固險，以拒豹子。

translations.literal: Wende relied on his troops and the rugged terrain to resist Baozi.
translations.idiomatic: Wende relied on his army and the rugged terrain to hold Baozi at bay.

sentences.zh: 文德將楊高來降，文德棄城南走，收其妻子寮屬及故武都王保宗妻公主送京師。

translations.literal: Wende's general Yang Gao came over in surrender; Wende abandoned the city and fled south, and Baozi took his wife, dependents, and retainers, together with the former Wudu king Baozong's wife the princess, and sent them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wende's general Yang Gao surrendered; Wende abandoned the city and fled south. Baozi seized his wife, household, and retainers, together with the former Wudu king Baozong's wife the princess, and sent them all to the capital.

sentences.zh: 宋白水太守郭啟玄率眾救文德，豹子大破之。

translations.literal: The Song Inspector of Baishui Guo Qixuan led troops to rescue Wende; Baozi inflicted a great defeat on him.
translations.idiomatic: The Song Inspector of Baishui, Guo Qixuan, led troops to rescue Wende, but Baozi routed him completely.

sentences.zh: 啟玄、文德走還漢中。

translations.literal: Qixuan and Wende fled back to Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Qixuan and Wende fled back to Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 興安二年，宋遣蕭道成等入漢中，別令楊文德、楊頭等率氐、羌圍武都。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xing'an, the Song sent Xiao Daocheng and others into Hanzhong and separately ordered Yang Wende and Yang Tou and others to lead the Di and Qiang in besieging Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xing'an, the Song sent Xiao Daocheng and others into Hanzhong and separately ordered Yang Wende, Yang Tou, and others to lead Di and Qiang forces in besieging Wudu.

sentences.zh: 豹子分兵將救之，聞宋人增兵益將，表狀求助。

translations.literal: Baozi divided his army to go to the rescue; hearing that the Song had increased troops and generals, he submitted a memorial requesting aid.
translations.idiomatic: Baozi divided his forces to relieve the siege; when he learned the Song were reinforcing their army, he submitted a memorial requesting help.

sentences.zh: 詔高平鎮將苟莫幹率突騎二千以赴之，道成等乃退。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Garrison Commander of Gaoping, Gou Mogan, to lead two thousand crack horsemen to his aid, and Daocheng and the others then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the Garrison Commander of Gaoping, Gou Mogan, to hurry to him with two thousand crack cavalry, and Daocheng and the others then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 征豹子為尚書，出為內都大官。

translations.literal: Baozi was summoned to the capital as Director of the Masters of Writing and then sent out as Grand Director of the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: Baozi was recalled to the capital as Director of the Masters of Writing and then sent out again as Grand Director of the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 宋遣其將殷孝祖修兩當城於清東，以逼南境。

translations.literal: The Song sent their general Yin Xiaozu to repair the Liangdang fortress on the Qing River to press the southern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The Song sent their general Yin Xiaozu to rebuild the Liangdang fortress on the Qing River to threaten the southern border.

sentences.zh: 天水公封敕文擊之，不克。

translations.literal: The Duke of Tianshui, Feng Chiwen, attacked him but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Tianshui, Feng Chiwen, attacked him but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 詔豹子與給事中周丘等助擊之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Baozi with the Attendant of Scattered Retainers Zhou Qiu and others to assist in the attack.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Baozi, together with the Attendant of Scattered Retainers Zhou Qiu and others, to assist in the attack.

sentences.zh: 宋瑕丘鎮遣步卒五千助戍兩當，豹子大破之。

translations.literal: The Song garrison of Xiaqiu sent five thousand foot soldiers to help defend Liangdang; Baozi inflicted a great defeat on them.
translations.idiomatic: The Song garrison at Xiaqiu sent five thousand foot soldiers to reinforce Liangdang; Baozi routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 追至城下，其免者千餘人而已。

translations.literal: He pursued to below the walls; only a little more than a thousand escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued to the walls of the fortress; barely more than a thousand men escaped.

sentences.zh: 既而班師。

translations.literal: Soon after he withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: He soon withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 先是，河西諸胡亡匿避命，豹子討之；

translations.literal: Before this, the various Hu of Hexi had fled and hidden to evade command; Baozi campaigned against them;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, various Hu peoples of Hexi had fled into hiding to evade imperial orders; Baozi campaigned against them;

sentences.zh: 不捷而還，又坐免官。

translations.literal: he did not succeed and returned, and again was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: he failed and withdrew, and was again dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 尋以前後戰功復擢為內都大官。

translations.literal: Soon, for his earlier and later battle achievements, he was again promoted to Grand Director of the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, for his earlier and later battle achievements, he was again promoted to Grand Director of the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 卒，文成追惜之，贈淮陽王，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: When he died, Emperor Wencheng mourned him with regret, posthumously made him Prince of Huaiyang, with the posthumous title Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, Emperor Wencheng mourned him with regret, posthumously made him Prince of Huaiyang, and gave him the posthumous title Xiang.

sentences.zh: 子道明襲。

translations.literal: His son Daoming inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daoming inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 道明第八弟懷喜，文成以其名臣子，擢為侍御中散，遷侍御長。

translations.literal: Daoming's eighth younger brother Huaixi—Emperor Wencheng, because he was the son of a renowned minister, promoted him to Attendant of Scattered Retainers in the Imperial Guard and transferred him to Chief of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Daoming's eighth younger brother Huaixi was, by Emperor Wencheng, raised from the son of a famous minister to Attendant of Scattered Retainers in the Imperial Guard and then to Chief of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 孝文初，吐谷渾拾夤部落饑窘，侵掠澆河。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, the Tuyuhun chieftain Shibin's tribes were hungry and distressed and raided Jiaohe.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, the Tuyuhun chieftain Shibin's tribes, hungry and desperate, raided Jiaohe.

sentences.zh: 詔假平西將軍、廣川公，與上党王長孫觀討拾夤。

translations.literal: An edict made him acting General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Guangchuan, and with the Prince of Shangdang, Zhangsun Guan, he campaigned against Shibin.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him acting General Who Pacifies the West and Duke of Guangchuan, and he campaigned against Shibin together with the Prince of Shangdang, Zhangsun Guan.

sentences.zh: 又以其父豹子昔鎮仇池，有威信，拜使持節、侍中、都督秦、雍、荊、梁、益五州諸軍事、本將軍、開府、仇池鎮將，假公如故。

translations.literal: Also, because his father Baozi had once garrisoned Chouchi and had prestige there, he was appointed Commissioner with the Staff, Attendant-in-Chief, Commander over the military affairs of Qin, Yong, Jing, Liang, and Yi provinces with his former general's title, Bearer of the Staff, Garrison Commander of Chouchi, and Duke in name as before.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father Baozi had once garrisoned Chouchi and enjoyed authority there, Huaixi was also appointed Commissioner with the Staff and Attendant-in-Chief, commander over military affairs in Qin, Yong, Jing, Liang, and Yi provinces with his former general's title, Bearer of the Staff, Garrison Commander of Chouchi, and duke in name as before.

sentences.zh: 懷喜至，申布恩惠。

translations.literal: When Huaixi arrived, he proclaimed favors and grace.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaixi arrived, he proclaimed the court's favors and grace.

sentences.zh: 夷人大悅，酋帥率戶歸附。

translations.literal: The barbarians were greatly pleased; their chieftains led their households to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes were greatly pleased, and their chieftains led their households in submission.

sentences.zh: 置廣業、固道二郡以居之。

translations.literal: The two commanderies of Guangye and Gudao were established to settle them.
translations.idiomatic: The commanderies of Guangye and Gudao were established to settle them.

sentences.zh: 徵為南部尚書，賜爵南康侯。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Director of the Masters of Writing for the South and granted the title Marquis of Nankang.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Director of the Masters of Writing for the South and enfeoffed as Marquis of Nankang.

sentences.zh: 封敕文，代人也，本姓是賁。

translations.literal: Feng Chiwen, a man of Dai, was originally surnamed Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Chiwen, a man of Dai, was originally of the surname Shi.

sentences.zh: 祖豆，位開府、冀青二州刺史、關內侯。

translations.literal: His grandfather Dou held the post of Bearer of the Staff, Inspector of Ji and Qing provinces, and Marquis Within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Dou had held the post of Bearer of the Staff, Inspector of Ji and Qing provinces, and Marquis Within the Passes.

sentences.zh: 父灊，侍御長，贈定州刺史、章武侯，諡曰隱。

translations.literal: His father Qian was Chief of the Imperial Guard; posthumously he was made Inspector of Dingzhou and Marquis of Zhangwu, with the posthumous title Yin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qian had been Chief of the Imperial Guard; after death he was posthumously appointed Inspector of Dingzhou and Marquis of Zhangwu, with the posthumous title Yin.

sentences.zh: 敕文始光初為中散，稍遷西部尚書，出為使持節、開府、領護西夷校尉、秦益二州刺史，賜爵天水公，鎮上邽。

translations.literal: Chiwen in the beginning of Shiguang was a Central Attendant, was gradually promoted to Director of the Masters of Writing for the West, and sent out as Commissioner with the Staff, Bearer of the Staff, Colonel Protecting the Western Yi, Inspector of Qin and Yi provinces, granted the title Duke of Tianshui, and stationed at Shanggui.
translations.idiomatic: Chiwen began as a Central Attendant in the Shiguang era, was gradually promoted to Director of the Masters of Writing for the West, and was then sent out as Commissioner with the Staff and Bearer of the Staff, Colonel Protecting the Western Yi, Inspector of Qin and Yi provinces, enfeoffed as Duke of Tianshui, and stationed at Shanggui.

sentences.zh: 詔敕文征吐谷渾慕利延兄子拾歸於枹罕。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Chiwen to campaign against Shigui, nephew of the Tuyuhun Muli Yan, at Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Chiwen to campaign against Shigui, nephew of the Tuyuhun ruler Muli Yan, at Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 眾少不制，詔廣川公乙烏頭等二軍與敕文會隴右。

translations.literal: His forces were few and could not control them; an edict ordered the armies of the Duke of Guangchuan, Yi Wutou, and others—two armies—to join Chiwen in Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: His force was too small to prevail; an edict ordered the two armies of the Duke of Guangchuan, Yi Wutou, and others to join Chiwen in Longyou.

sentences.zh: 軍次武始，拾歸夜遁，敕文引軍入枹罕，虜拾歸妻子及其人戶，分徙千家於上邽，留烏頭守桴罕。

translations.literal: When the army reached Wuzhi, Shigui fled by night; Chiwen led the army into Fuhan, captured Shigui's wife and children and their households, moved a thousand households to Shanggui, and left Wutou to guard Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Wuzhi, Shigui fled by night. Chiwen advanced into Fuhan, seized Shigui's wife, children, and households, resettled a thousand households at Shanggui, and left Wutou to guard Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 金城邊冏，天水梁會謀反，據上邽東城南城，攻逼西城。

translations.literal: Bian Tong of Jincheng and Liang Hui of Tianshui plotted rebellion, holding the eastern and southern walls of Shanggui and pressing the western wall.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Tong of Jincheng and Liang Hui of Tianshui rose in rebellion, seized the eastern and southern walls of Shanggui, and attacked the western wall.

sentences.zh: 敕文先已設備，賊乃退。

translations.literal: Chiwen had already made preparations, and the rebels withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Chiwen had already made his preparations, and the rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 冏、會復攻城，氐、羌一萬屯南嶺，休官、屠各及雜戶二萬餘人屯北嶺，為冏等形援。

translations.literal: Tong and Hui again attacked the city; ten thousand Di and Qiang encamped on the southern ridge, and more than twenty thousand Xiuguan, Tujue, and miscellaneous households encamped on the northern ridge to support Tong and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Tong and Hui attacked the city again. Ten thousand Di and Qiang encamped on the southern ridge, while more than twenty thousand Xiuguan, Tujue, and miscellaneous households encamped on the northern ridge to support them.

sentences.zh: 敕文設奇兵大破之，斬冏。

translations.literal: Chiwen set an ambush and inflicted a great defeat, beheading Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Chiwen laid an ambush and won a crushing victory, beheading Tong.

sentences.zh: 眾復推梁會為主。

translations.literal: The masses again set up Liang Hui as leader.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels again made Liang Hui their leader.

sentences.zh: 安豐公閭根率軍助敕文，敕文又表求助，未及報。

translations.literal: The Duke of Anfeng, Lu Gen, led troops to assist Chiwen; Chiwen also submitted a memorial requesting aid, but before a reply arrived—
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Anfeng, Lu Gen, led troops to assist Chiwen, and Chiwen also submitted a memorial requesting reinforcements, but no reply had yet arrived.

sentences.zh: 梁會欲謀逃遁。

translations.literal: Liang Hui wished to plot escape.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Hui planned to flee.

sentences.zh: 先是敕文掘重塹於東城之外，幾斷賊走路。

translations.literal: Earlier Chiwen had dug a deep moat outside the eastern wall, nearly cutting off the rebels' escape route.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Chiwen had dug a deep moat outside the eastern wall, nearly cutting off the rebels' line of retreat.

sentences.zh: 夜半，會乃飛梯騰塹而走。

translations.literal: At midnight Hui used flying ladders to leap the moat and flee.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight Hui used flying ladders to vault the moat and escape.

sentences.zh: 敕文先嚴兵於塹外，拒鬥，從夜至旦。

translations.literal: Chiwen had already drawn up his troops outside the moat to resist; the fighting lasted from night until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Chiwen had already drawn up his troops outside the moat to block them, and the fighting lasted from night until dawn.

sentences.zh: 敕文謀於眾曰：「困獸猶鬥，而況於人。

translations.literal: Chiwen said to the assembly, "A cornered beast will still fight—how much more so a man.
translations.idiomatic: Chiwen said to his officers, "A cornered beast will still fight—how much more will men do so.

sentences.zh: 」乃以白武幡宣告賊眾，若能歸降，原其生命，應時降者六百餘人。

translations.literal: " He then proclaimed to the rebel masses with a white martial banner that those who submitted would be spared their lives; more than six hundred surrendered at once.
translations.idiomatic: " He then raised a white martial banner and proclaimed to the rebel ranks that those who submitted would be spared; more than six hundred men surrendered on the spot.

sentences.zh: 會知人心沮壞，於是分遁。

translations.literal: Hui knew that hearts were broken, and thereupon the force scattered in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that morale had collapsed, Hui broke his force apart and fled in every direction.

sentences.zh: 敕文縱騎騰躡，死者太半。

translations.literal: Chiwen sent cavalry in pursuit; more than half the rebels were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Chiwen sent cavalry in pursuit, and more than half the rebels were killed.

sentences.zh: 呂羅漢，本東平壽張人也，其先石勒時徙居幽州。

translations.literal: Lu Luohan was originally a man of Shouzhang in Dongping; his ancestors in the time of Shi Le had been moved to Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Luohan was originally from Shouzhang in Dongping; his ancestors had been relocated to Youzhou in the time of Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 祖顯，字子明。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xian, styled Ziming.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xian was styled Ziming.

sentences.zh: 少好學，性廉直，鄉人有忿爭者皆就質焉。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and was upright by nature; when fellow villagers had quarrels they all came to him for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning and was upright by nature; when neighbors quarreled they all came to him for judgment.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂以為河間太守。

translations.literal: Murong Chui made him Inspector of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui appointed him Inspector of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 皇始初，以郡降，道武賜爵魏昌男。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangshi, he submitted the commandery and was granted the title Baron of Weichang by Emperor Daowu.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Huangshi era he surrendered the commandery to the Wei court, and Emperor Daowu enfeoffed him as Baron of Weichang.

sentences.zh: 拜钜鹿太守。

translations.literal: He was appointed Inspector of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Inspector of Julu.

sentences.zh: 清身奉公，妻子不免饑寒，百姓頌之曰：「時惟府君，克清克明，緝我荒土，人胥樂生，願壽無疆，以享長齡。

translations.literal: He kept his person pure and served the public; his wife and children did not escape hunger and cold, and the people praised him saying, "In this age our prefect is pure and bright; he has brought order to our wasted land, and all rejoice in life—we wish him long years without end, to enjoy a full span.
translations.idiomatic: He lived plainly in service of the public good; his wife and children still knew hunger and cold, yet the people praised him in verse: "In this age our prefect is pure and bright; he has brought order to our wasted land, and all rejoice in life—we wish him endless years to enjoy a full span.

sentences.zh: 」卒官。

translations.literal: " He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: " He died in office.

sentences.zh: 父溫，字晞陽。

translations.literal: His father Wen, styled Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wen was styled Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 善書，好施，有文武才略。

translations.literal: He was skilled at calligraphy, generous in giving, and had both civil and military talent.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in calligraphy, generous in giving, and possessed both civil and military ability.

sentences.zh: 位上党太守，有能名。

translations.literal: He held the post of Inspector of Shangdang and was known for ability.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Inspector of Shangdang and was known for his ability.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈豫州刺史、野王侯，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made Inspector of Yuzhou and Marquis of Yewang, with the posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously appointed Inspector of Yuzhou and Marquis of Yewang, with the posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 羅漢仁厚篤慎，弱冠以武幹知名。

translations.literal: Luohan was benevolent, generous, and careful; from his weak-capped years he was known for martial talent.
translations.idiomatic: Luohan was benevolent, generous, and careful; from his youth he was known for martial ability.

sentences.zh: 父溫之為秦州司馬，羅漢隨侍。

translations.literal: When his father Wen was Military Assistant of Qinzhou, Luohan accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: When his father Wen served as Military Assistant of Qinzhou, Luohan accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 隴右氐楊難當寇上邽，鎮將元意頭知羅漢善射，共登西城樓令射。

translations.literal: The Di of Longyou, Yang Nan'dang, raided Shanggui; the Garrison Commander Yuan Yitou, knowing Luohan was skilled at archery, climbed the western city tower with him and had him shoot.
translations.idiomatic: The Di chieftain Yang Nan'dang of Longyou raided Shanggui; the garrison commander Yuan Yitou, knowing Luohan was an expert archer, climbed the western city tower with him and had him shoot.

sentences.zh: 難當隊將及兵二十三人應弦而殪。

translations.literal: Nan'dang's squad commanders and soldiers—twenty-three men—fell to the bowstring.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-three of Nan'dang's squad commanders and soldiers fell to Luohan's bow in succession.

sentences.zh: 賊眾轉盛，羅漢曰：「今不出戰，示敵以弱。

translations.literal: The rebel force grew stronger; Luohan said, "If we do not go out to battle now, we show the enemy weakness.
translations.idiomatic: As the enemy force grew, Luohan said, "If we do not fight now, we show them we are weak.

sentences.zh: 」意頭善之，即簡千餘人，令羅漢出戰，眾皆披靡。

translations.literal: " Yitou approved, immediately selected more than a thousand men, and ordered Luohan out to battle; the masses were all routed.
translations.idiomatic: " Yitou approved, immediately picked out more than a thousand men, and sent Luohan to attack; the enemy ranks broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 難當大驚，會太武賜難當璽書，責其跋扈，難當還仇池。

translations.literal: Nan'dang was greatly alarmed; just then Emperor Taiwu sent Nan'dang an imperial letter reproaching his arrogance, and Nan'dang returned to Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: Nan'dang was greatly alarmed. Just then Emperor Taiwu sent him an imperial letter reproaching his arrogance, and Nan'dang withdrew to Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 意頭具以狀聞，徵為羽林郎。

translations.literal: Yitou reported the full circumstances; Luohan was summoned as a Guard of the Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: Yitou reported the full account to the court, and Luohan was summoned to serve as a Guard of the Feathered Forest.

sentences.zh: 上邽休官呂豐、屠各、王飛鹿等據險為逆，詔羅漢討禽之。

translations.literal: The Xiuguan Lu Feng, Tujue, Wang Feilu, and others of Shanggui held rugged terrain in rebellion; an edict ordered Luohan to campaign and capture them.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiuguan Lu Feng, Tujue chieftains, Wang Feilu, and others of Shanggui held rugged ground in rebellion; an edict ordered Luohan to campaign against them and take them captive.

sentences.zh: 後從征懸瓠，以功遷羽林中郎、幢將，賜爵烏程子。

translations.literal: Later he followed the expedition against Xuanchi and for his merit was transferred to Captain of the Feathered Forest and Standard Bearer, granted the title Baron of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined the expedition against Xuanchi and, for his merit, was promoted to Captain of the Feathered Forest and Standard Bearer, enfeoffed as Baron of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 及南安王余立，羅漢猶典宿衛，文成之立，羅漢有力焉。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Nan'an, Yu, was established, Luohan still directed the night guard; in Emperor Wencheng's establishment Luohan had a strong hand.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Nan'an, Yu, was enthroned, Luohan still directed the night guard; he had played an important part in Emperor Wencheng's accession as well.

sentences.zh: 加龍驤將軍，仍幢將，進爵野王侯，拜司衛監。

translations.literal: He was made General of the Dragon Cavalry, still Standard Bearer, advanced to Marquis of Yewang, and appointed Director of Palace Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General of the Dragon Cavalry while retaining his post as Standard Bearer, advanced to Marquis of Yewang, and appointed Director of Palace Guards.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍、殿中尚書，進爵山陽公。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Palace Secretariat, advancing to Duke of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Palace Secretariat, advancing to Duke of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 後為鎮西將軍、秦、益二州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was made General Who Guards the West and Inspector of Qin and Yi provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made General Who Guards the West and Inspector of Qin and Yi provinces.

sentences.zh: 時仇池氐、羌反，逼駱穀，鎮將吳保元走登百頃，請援于羅漢族。

translations.literal: At that time the Di and Qiang of Chouchi rebelled, pressing Luogu; the Garrison Commander Wu Baoyuan fled up to Baizhang and requested aid from Luohan's command.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Di and Qiang of Chouchi rebelled and pressed Luogu; the garrison commander Wu Baoyuan retreated to Baizhang and requested aid from Luohan's forces.

sentences.zh: 羅漢帥步騎隨長孫觀，掩擊氐、羌大破之，賊眾退散。

translations.literal: Luohan led foot and horse with Zhangsun Guan in a surprise attack and inflicted a great defeat on the Di and Qiang; the rebel masses dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Luohan led infantry and cavalry with Zhangsun Guan in a surprise attack, routed the Di and Qiang completely, and the rebels dispersed.

sentences.zh: 詔書慰勉之。

translations.literal: An edict comforted and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict arrived comforting and encouraging him.

sentences.zh: 涇州人張羌郎聚眾千人，州軍討之。

translations.literal: Zhang Qianglang of Jingzhou gathered a force of a thousand men; the provincial army campaigned against him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qianglang of Jingzhou gathered a force of a thousand men, and the provincial army campaigned against him.

sentences.zh: 不能制，羅漢擊禽之。

translations.literal: They could not control him; Luohan attacked and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: They could not subdue him; Luohan attacked and took him captive.

sentences.zh: 仇池氐、羌叛逆。

translations.literal: The Di and Qiang of Chouchi rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The Di and Qiang of Chouchi rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 其賊帥蛩廉、苻忻等皆受宋官爵鐵券。

translations.literal: Their rebel leaders Qiong Lian, Fu Xin, and others had all received Song offices, titles, and iron bonds of assurance.
translations.idiomatic: Their leaders Qiong Lian, Fu Xin, and others had all received Song offices, titles, and iron bonds of assurance.

sentences.zh: 略陽公伏阿奴為都將，與羅漢赴討，所在破之，禽廉、忻等。

translations.literal: The Duke of Lueyang, Fu Anu, was commander and campaigned with Luohan; wherever they went they broke the enemy and captured Lian, Xin, and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Lueyang, Fu Anu, served as commander and campaigned with Luohan; wherever they advanced they broke the enemy and captured Lian, Xin, and the others.

sentences.zh: 秦、益阻遠，南連仇池，西接赤水，諸羌恃險，數為叛逆，自羅漢蒞州，撫以威惠，西戎懷德，土境怗然。

translations.literal: Qin and Yi were remote, bordering Chouchi to the south and Chishui to the west; the various Qiang relied on the terrain and repeatedly rebelled, but from the time Luohan took the province he governed them with authority and kindness—the western tribes submitted in gratitude and the territory was at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Yi were remote provinces, bordering Chouchi to the south and the Chishui region to the west. The Qiang tribes there relied on rugged terrain and rebelled repeatedly, but from the time Luohan took office he governed them with both authority and kindness; the western tribes submitted in gratitude and the borderlands were tranquil.

sentences.zh: 孝文下詔褒美之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen issued an edict praising him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen issued an edict praising his service.

sentences.zh: 徵拜內都大官，聽察多得其情。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Grand Director of the Inner Court and in hearing cases often got to the truth.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Grand Director of the Inner Court and in hearing cases often got to the heart of the matter.

sentences.zh: 卒官，諡莊公。

translations.literal: He died in office; his posthumous title was Duke Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously known as Duke Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 長子興祖襲爵山陽公，後例降為侯。

translations.literal: His eldest son Xingzu inherited the title Duke of Shanyang; later by regulation it was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Xingzu inherited the title Duke of Shanyang; later, under the usual regulation, the rank was reduced to marquis.

sentences.zh: 孔伯恭，魏郡鄴人也。

translations.literal: Kong Bogong was a man of Ye in Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Bogong was from Ye in Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 父昭，位侍中、幽州刺中、魯郡公。

translations.literal: His father Zhao held the posts of Attendant-in-Chief, Inspector of Youzhou, and Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhao had served as Attendant-in-Chief, Inspector of Youzhou, and Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰康。

translations.literal: When he died his posthumous title was Kang.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously known as Kang.

sentences.zh: 伯恭以父任拜給事中，後賜爵濟陽男，進彭城公。

translations.literal: Bogong through his father's position was appointed Attendant of Scattered Retainers; later he was granted the title Baron of Jiyang and advanced to Duke of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's standing Bogong was appointed Attendant of Scattered Retainers; he was later enfeoffed as Baron of Jiyang and advanced to Duke of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 獻文初，宋徐州刺史薛安都以彭城內附。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xianwen's reign, the Song Inspector of Xuzhou Xue Andu submitted Pengcheng to the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xianwen's reign, the Song Inspector of Xuzhou, Xue Andu, surrendered Pengcheng to the Wei.

sentences.zh: 宋遣將張永、沈攸之等擊安都。

translations.literal: The Song sent the generals Zhang Yong and Shen Youzhi and others to attack Andu.
translations.idiomatic: The Song sent generals Zhang Yong, Shen Youzhi, and others to attack Andu.

sentences.zh: 安都請援，獻文進伯恭號鎮東將軍，副尚書尉元救之。

translations.literal: Andu requested aid; Emperor Xianwen advanced Bogong to General Who Pacifies the East and had him assist the Director of the Masters of Writing Yu Yuan in the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Andu requested aid; Emperor Xianwen promoted Bogong to General Who Pacifies the East and sent him to assist the Director of the Masters of Writing Yu Yuan in the relief effort.

sentences.zh: 永與攸之棄船而走。

translations.literal: Yong and Youzhi abandoned their boats and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yong and Youzhi abandoned their boats and fled.

sentences.zh: 伯恭以書喻下邳、宿豫城內。

translations.literal: Bogong by letter persuaded the garrisons within Xiapi and Suyu to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Bogong persuaded the garrisons of Xiapi and Suyu to submit by letter.

sentences.zh: 時攸之、吳喜公等率眾來援下邳，屯軍焦墟曲，去下邳五十餘里。

translations.literal: At that time Youzhi, the Duke of Wu Xi, and others led troops to relieve Xiapi, encamping at Jiaoxu Qu, more than fifty li from Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi, the Duke of Wu Xi, and others then led troops to relieve Xiapi, encamping at Jiaoxu Qu, a little more than fifty li from the city.

sentences.zh: 伯恭密造火車攻其營，水陸俱進。

translations.literal: Bogong secretly built fire carts to attack their camp, advancing by land and water together.
translations.idiomatic: Bogong secretly built fire carts to attack their camp, advancing by land and water at once.

sentences.zh: 攸之等既聞將戰，引軍退保樊階城。

translations.literal: Youzhi and the others, hearing that battle was imminent, withdrew their army to defend Fanjie city.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi and the others, hearing that battle was imminent, withdrew to defend Fanjie city.

sentences.zh: 宋甯朔將軍陳顯達領眾溯清而上，以迎攸之；

translations.literal: The Song General Who Pacifies the North Chen Xianda led troops up the Qing River to meet Youzhi;
translations.idiomatic: The Song General Who Pacifies the North, Chen Xianda, led troops up the Qing River to join Youzhi;

sentences.zh: 屯于睢、清合口。

translations.literal: he encamped at the confluence of the Sui and Qing rivers.
translations.idiomatic: he encamped where the Sui and Qing rivers met.

sentences.zh: 伯恭率眾度水，大破顯達。

translations.literal: Bogong led his troops across the water and inflicted a great defeat on Xianda.
translations.idiomatic: Bogong led his troops across the river and routed Xianda completely.

sentences.zh: 攸之聞顯達軍敗，順流退下。

translations.literal: Youzhi, hearing that Xianda's army had been defeated, withdrew downstream.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhi learned that Xianda's army had been defeated, he withdrew downstream.

sentences.zh: 伯恭從清西與攸之合戰，大破之，吳喜公輕騎遁走。

translations.literal: Bogong from the west bank of the Qing joined battle with Youzhi and inflicted a great defeat; the Duke of Wu Xi fled on light horse.
translations.idiomatic: Bogong attacked from the west bank of the Qing, joined battle with Youzhi, and won a crushing victory; the Duke of Wu Xi fled on a light horse.

sentences.zh: 乘勝追奔八十餘里，軍資器械虜獲萬計。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory in pursuit for more than eighty li, they captured military supplies and equipment by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the victory, they pursued for more than eighty li and captured military supplies and equipment by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 進攻宿豫，宋戍將魯僧遵棄城夜遁。

translations.literal: They advanced to attack Suyu; the Song garrison commander Lu Zongzun abandoned the city and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: They advanced against Suyu; the Song garrison commander Lu Zongzun abandoned the city and fled by night.

sentences.zh: 又遣將孔大恆等南討淮陽，宋太守崔武仲焚城南走，遂據淮陽。

translations.literal: He also sent the generals Kong Daheng and others south to campaign against Huaiyang; the Song prefect Cui Wuzhong burned the city and fled south, and they then held Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent generals Kong Daheng and others south against Huaiyang; the Song prefect Cui Wuzhong burned the southern part of the city and fled, and the Wei forces then took Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 皇興二年，以伯恭為散騎常侍、彭城鎮將、都督徐南北兗州諸軍事，假東海公。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangxing, Bogong was made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Garrison Commander of Pengcheng, and Commander over the military affairs of Xu, the northern and southern parts of Xu, and Yan provinces, with the title Duke of Donghai in name.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huangxing, Bogong was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Garrison Commander of Pengcheng, and commander over military affairs in Xu province and the northern and southern districts of Xu and Yan, with the title Duke of Donghai in name.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈鎮東大將軍、東海王，諡曰桓。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East and Prince of Donghai, with the posthumous title Huan.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Prince of Donghai, with the posthumous title Huan.

sentences.zh: 伯恭弟伯遜，襲父爵魯郡公，位東萊鎮將、東徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Bogong's younger brother Boxun inherited his father's title Duke of Lu and held the posts of Garrison Commander of Donglai and Inspector of Dongxu.
translations.idiomatic: Bogong's younger brother Boxun inherited their father's title Duke of Lu and served as Garrison Commander of Donglai and Inspector of Dongxu.

sentences.zh: 坐事免官，卒於家。

translations.literal: He was dismissed from office for an offense and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed from office for an offense and died at home.

sentences.zh: 田益宗，光城蠻也。

translations.literal: Tian Yizong was a Man of Guangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yizong was a Man chieftain of Guangcheng.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，雄果有將略，貌狀舉止，有異常蠻。

translations.literal: He stood eight chi tall, was bold and had military talent; his appearance and bearing were unlike ordinary Man.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight chi tall, was bold and possessed real military talent, and his appearance and bearing were unlike those of ordinary Man tribesmen.

sentences.zh: 世為四山蠻帥，受制于齊。

translations.literal: His family for generations had been chieftains of the Four Mountains Man, subject to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His family had for generations been chieftains of the Four Mountains Man, subject to Qi.

sentences.zh: 太和十七年，遣使張超奉表歸魏。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Taihe he sent the envoy Zhang Chao to submit a memorial and return to Wei allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Taihe he sent the envoy Zhang Chao with a memorial submitting to Wei allegiance.

sentences.zh: 十九年，拜員外散騎常侍、都督、南司州刺史、光城縣伯，食蠻邑一千戶，所統守宰，任其銓置。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Commander, Inspector of Southern Sizhou, and Baron of Guangcheng with a fief of a thousand Man households; the garrison commanders under his authority he was permitted to appoint and remove.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was appointed Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, commander, and Inspector of Southern Sizhou, enfeoffed as Baron of Guangcheng with a fief of a thousand Man households; the garrison commanders under his command he was permitted to appoint and remove at will.

sentences.zh: 後以益宗既度淮北，不可仍為司州，乃于新蔡立東豫州，以益宗為刺史。

translations.literal: Later, because Yizong had already crossed north of the Huai, he could not still hold Sizhou; Eastern Yuzhou was therefore established at Xincai with Yizong as inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because Yizong had already crossed north of the Huai, he could no longer hold Sizhou; the court therefore established Eastern Yuzhou at Xincai and appointed Yizong its inspector.

sentences.zh: 尋改封安昌縣伯。

translations.literal: Soon his title was changed to Baron of Anchang.
translations.idiomatic: His title was soon changed to Baron of Anchang.

sentences.zh: 景明初，梁師寇三關，益宗遣光城太守楊興之進至陰山關。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming, Liang forces raided the Three Passes; Yizong sent the Administrator of Guangcheng Yang Xingzhi to advance to Yinshan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingming era, Liang forces raided the Three Passes; Yizong sent the Administrator of Guangcheng, Yang Xingzhi, to advance to Yinshan Pass.

sentences.zh: 南據長風城，逆擊大破之。

translations.literal: He moved south to hold Changfeng city and met the enemy in a counterattack, inflicting a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzhi moved south to hold Changfeng city, met the enemy in a counterattack, and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 梁建甯太守黃天賜築城赤亭，復遣其將黃公賞屯於漴城，與長風相持。

translations.literal: The Liang Inspector of Jianning Huang Tianci built a fortress at Chiting; he again sent his general Huang Gongshang to garrison Chong city in support of Changfeng.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang Inspector of Jianning, Huang Tianci, built a fortress at Chiting and again sent his general Huang Gongshang to garrison Chong city in support of Changfeng.

sentences.zh: 益宗命安蠻太守梅景秀與興之掎角擊討。

translations.literal: Yizong ordered the Administrator Who Pacifies the Man Mei Jingxiu and Xingzhi to attack from two sides.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong ordered the Administrator Who Pacifies the Man, Mei Jingxiu, and Xingzhi to attack from two sides.

sentences.zh: 破之，獲其二城。

translations.literal: They defeated them and took the two cities.
translations.idiomatic: They defeated the Liang forces and captured both cities.

sentences.zh: 上表陳攻取之術。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial setting forth the methods of attack and capture.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong submitted a memorial setting forth his methods of attack and capture.

sentences.zh: 宣武納之，遣鎮南將軍元英攻義陽。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu accepted it and sent the General Who Guards the South Yuan Ying to attack Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu accepted the plan and sent the General Who Guards the South, Yuan Ying, to attack Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 益宗遣其息魯生斷梁人糧運，破梁戍主趙文興，倉米運舟，焚燒蕩盡。

translations.literal: Yizong sent his son Lusheng to cut the Liang grain transport, defeated the Liang garrison commander Zhao Wenxing, and burned all the grain stored in warehouses and transported by boat.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong sent his son Lusheng to cut the Liang grain supply line, defeated the Liang garrison commander Zhao Wenxing, and burned all the grain in storehouses and transport boats.

sentences.zh: 時樂口已南，郢、豫二州諸縣皆沒于梁，唯有義陽而已。

translations.literal: At that time south of Lekou, the counties of Ying and Yu provinces had all fallen to Liang; only Yiyang remained.
translations.idiomatic: By then every county of Ying and Yu provinces south of Lekou had fallen to Liang; only Yiyang remained.

sentences.zh: 梁招益宗以車騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、五千戶郡公。

translations.literal: Liang tried to win Yizong with the offer of Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Bearer of the Staff with the Same Powers as the Three Excellencies, and Duke of a commandery with five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Liang tried to win Yizong over with an offer of Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Bearer of the Staff with the Same Powers as the Three Excellencies, and the title Duke of a five-thousand-household commandery.

sentences.zh: 當時安危在益宗去就，而益宗守節不移，郢、豫克平，益宗力也。

translations.literal: At that time the safety of the realm hung on whether Yizong would stay or go, yet Yizong held to his loyalty without wavering; the pacification of Ying and Yu was largely his doing.
translations.idiomatic: The safety of the realm then hung on whether Yizong would stay or go, yet he held to his loyalty without wavering; the recovery of Ying and Yu was largely his achievement.

sentences.zh: 益宗年稍衰老，聚斂無厭。

translations.literal: As Yizong grew older he amassed wealth without satiety.
translations.idiomatic: As Yizong grew older he amassed wealth without satiety.

sentences.zh: 兵人患其侵擾，諸子及孫，競規賄貨。

translations.literal: The soldiers resented his exactions; his sons and grandsons all competed for bribes.
translations.idiomatic: His soldiers resented his exactions, and his sons and grandsons all competed for bribes.

sentences.zh: 部內苦之，咸言欲叛。

translations.literal: Those within his commandery suffered bitterly and all said they wished to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: The people under his command suffered bitterly and openly spoke of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 宣武深亦慮焉，乃遣中書舍人劉桃符宣旨慰喻，庶以安之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu was deeply concerned as well; he sent the Attendant of the Masters of Writing Liu Taofu with an imperial message to comfort and instruct him, hoping thereby to settle matters.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu was deeply concerned as well; he sent the Attendant of the Masters of Writing Liu Taofu with an imperial message to comfort and instruct him, hoping thereby to restore calm.

sentences.zh: 桃符還，啟益宗侵掠之狀。

translations.literal: When Taofu returned he reported Yizong's acts of plunder.
translations.idiomatic: When Taofu returned he reported Yizong's acts of plunder to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔之曰：「聞卿息魯生在淮南貪暴，橫殺梅伏生，為爾不已，損卿誠效，可會魯生與使赴闕，當加任使。

translations.literal: An edict said to him, "We have heard that your son Lusheng in Huainan is greedy and violent and has wantonly killed Mei Fusheng, to your endless discredit and harm to your loyal service. You should have Lusheng meet the envoy and come to court; he will receive appointment and employment.
translations.idiomatic: An edict addressed him: "We have heard that your son Lusheng in Huainan is greedy and violent and has wantonly killed Mei Fusheng, to your endless discredit and harm to your loyal service. Have Lusheng meet the envoy and come to court; he will receive appointment and employment."

sentences.zh: 」魯生久未至。

translations.literal: " Lusheng long did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: " Lusheng did not arrive for a long time.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，詔以益宗為使持節、鎮東將軍、濟州刺史，常侍如故。

translations.literal: In the Yan-chang era an edict made Yizong Commissioner with the Staff, General Who Pacifies the East, and Inspector of Jizhou, with Attendant-in-Chief as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yan-chang era an edict appointed Yizong Commissioner with the Staff, General Who Pacifies the East, and Inspector of Jizhou, retaining his post as Attendant-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 帝慮其不受代，遣後將軍李世哲與桃符率從襲之，奄入廣陵。

translations.literal: The emperor feared he would not accept transfer; he sent the Rear General Li Shizhe with Taofu to lead followers in a surprise attack, suddenly entering Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feared Yizong would refuse transfer and sent the Rear General Li Shizhe with Taofu to lead a surprise force that suddenly entered Guangling.

sentences.zh: 益宗子魯生、魯賢等奔于關南，招引梁兵，光城已南，皆為梁所保。

translations.literal: Yizong's sons Lusheng, Luxian, and others fled south of the passes, drew in Liang troops, and from Guangcheng southward all was held by Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong's sons Lusheng and Luxian fled south of the passes, drew in Liang troops, and from Guangcheng southward the territory fell under Liang control.

sentences.zh: 世哲擊破之，復置郡戍，以益宗還。

translations.literal: Shizhe defeated them, re-established commandery garrisons, and returned Yizong to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhe defeated them, re-established commandery garrisons, and restored Yizong to his post.

sentences.zh: 授征南將軍、金紫光祿大夫，加散騎常侍，改封曲陽縣伯。

translations.literal: He was given General Who Conquers the South, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, with the additional title Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and his title was changed to Baron of Quyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Conquers the South and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, with the additional title Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and his enfeoffment was changed to Baron of Quyang.

sentences.zh: 益宗生長邊地，不願內榮，雖位秩崇重，猶以為恨，表陳桃符讒毀之狀。

translations.literal: Yizong had grown up on the frontier and did not desire inner glory; though his rank was lofty and heavy he still harbored resentment and submitted a memorial setting forth Taofu's slander.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong had grown up on the frontier and did not crave honors at court; though his rank was lofty he still resented Taofu's slander and submitted a memorial setting it forth.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「既經大宥，不容方更為獄。

translations.literal: An edict said, "Since there has already been a great pardon, it is not fitting to reopen the matter in court.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied, "Since a general pardon has already been granted, the matter cannot be reopened in court."

sentences.zh: 」熙平初，益宗又表乞東豫，以招二子。

translations.literal: " At the beginning of Xiping, Yizong again memorialized requesting Eastern Yuzhou to win back his two sons.
translations.idiomatic: " At the beginning of the Xiping era Yizong again memorialized requesting Eastern Yuzhou to win back his two sons.

sentences.zh: 靈太后令答不許。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling ordered a reply refusing permission.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling ordered a reply refusing.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈征東大將軍、郢州刺史，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made General Who Conquers the East and Inspector of Yingzhou, with the posthumous title Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously appointed General Who Conquers the East and Inspector of Yingzhou, with the posthumous title Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 少子纂襲，位中散大夫，卒，贈東豫州刺史。

translations.literal: His youngest son Zuan inherited; he held the post of Supernumerary Attendant of Scattered Retainers and when he died was posthumously made Inspector of Eastern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Zuan inherited the line; he served as Supernumerary Attendant of Scattered Retainers and after death was posthumously appointed Inspector of Eastern Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 益宗長子隨興，位弋陽、東汝南二郡太守。

translations.literal: Yizong's eldest son Suixing held the posts of Inspector of the two commanderies of Yiyang and Eastern Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong's eldest son Suixing served as inspector of Yiyang and Eastern Runan commanderies.

sentences.zh: 益宗兄興祖，位江州刺史。

translations.literal: Yizong's elder brother Xingzu held the post of Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong's elder brother Xingzu served as Inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 孟表，字武達，濟北蛇丘人也。

translations.literal: Meng Biao, styled Wuda, was a man of Sheqiu in Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Biao, styled Wuda, was from Sheqiu in Jibei.

sentences.zh: 自雲本屬北地，號索裏諸孟。

translations.literal: By his own account his family originally belonged to Beidi and were called the various Meng of Suoli.
translations.idiomatic: By his own account his clan originally came from Beidi and were known as the various Meng of Suoli.

sentences.zh: 青、徐內屬後，表因事南度，仕齊為馬頭太守。

translations.literal: After Qing and Xu submitted within, Biao because of events crossed south and served Qi as Inspector of Matou.
translations.idiomatic: After Qing and Xu submitted to the Wei, Biao crossed south because of circumstances and served Qi as Administrator of Matou.

sentences.zh: 太和十八年，表據郡歸魏，除南兗州刺史，領馬頭太守，賜爵譙縣侯，鎮渦陽。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Taihe, Biao held the commandery and returned to Wei; he was made Inspector of Southern Yanzhou, concurrently Administrator of Matou, granted the title Marquis of Qiao, and stationed at Woyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Taihe, Biao held his commandery and submitted to Wei; he was appointed Inspector of Southern Yanzhou and concurrent Administrator of Matou, enfeoffed as Marquis of Qiao, and stationed at Woyang.

sentences.zh: 後齊遣其豫州刺史裴叔業攻圍六十餘日，城中食盡，唯以朽革及草木皮葉為糧。

translations.literal: Later Qi sent their Inspector of Yuzhou Pei Shuye to attack and besiege the city for more than sixty days; food in the city was exhausted and they had only rotten leather and the bark and leaves of plants and trees for provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qi sent their Inspector of Yuzhou, Pei Shuye, to besiege the city for more than sixty days. When food ran out, the defenders ate only rotten leather and the bark and leaves of plants and trees.

sentences.zh: 表撫循將士，戮力固守。

translations.literal: Biao comforted and guided the officers and men and strove together to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: Biao comforted his officers and men and strove with them to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 會鎮南將軍王肅救之，叔業乃退。

translations.literal: Just then the General Who Guards the South Wang Su came to the rescue and Shuye then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the General Who Guards the South, Wang Su, came to relieve the siege, and Shuye withdrew.

sentences.zh: 初，有一南人，自雲姓邊字叔珍，攜妻息從壽春投表，未及送闕，會叔業圍城。

translations.literal: At first there was a southerner who claimed the surname Bian and the style Shuzhen, bringing wife and children from Shouchun to join Biao; before he could be sent to court, Shuye besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: At first a southerner who gave his surname as Bian and his style as Shuzhen arrived from Shouchun with wife and children to join Biao; before he could be sent to court, Shuye besieged the city.

sentences.zh: 表後察叔珍言色頗有異，即推核，乃是叔業姑兒，規為內應。

translations.literal: Later Biao observed that Shuzhen's words and expression were rather strange and immediately investigated; he was in fact Shuye's cousin by the female line and had planned to serve as an inside agent.
translations.idiomatic: Later Biao noticed something odd in Shuzhen's words and bearing and investigated at once; he turned out to be Shuye's cousin on the maternal side and had planned to act as an inside agent.

sentences.zh: 所攜妻子，並亦假妄，於北門外斬之，人情乃安。

translations.literal: The wife and children he had brought were also false; they were beheaded outside the north gate and popular feeling was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: The wife and children he had brought were impostors as well; they were beheaded outside the north gate, and public feeling was then settled.

sentences.zh: 孝文嘉其誠，封汶陽縣伯，曆濟州刺史、散騎常侍、光祿大夫、齊州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen praised his loyalty and enfeoffed him as Baron of Wenyang; he successively held the posts of Inspector of Jizhou, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Inspector of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen praised his loyalty and enfeoffed him as Baron of Wenyang; he served in turn as Inspector of Jizhou, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Inspector of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈兗州刺史，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made Inspector of Yanzhou, with the posthumous title Gong.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously appointed Inspector of Yanzhou, with the posthumous title Gong.

sentences.zh: 奚康生，河南陽翟人也。

translations.literal: Xi Kangsheng was a man of Yangzhai in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Kangsheng was from Yangzhai in Henan.

sentences.zh: 本姓達奚，其先居代，世為部落大人。

translations.literal: His original surname was Daxi; his ancestors dwelt in Dai and for generations were great chiefs of the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: His original surname was Daxi; his ancestors had dwelt in Dai and for generations were great chiefs of the tribes.

sentences.zh: 祖真，柔玄鎮將、內外三都大官，賜爵長進侯。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhen was Garrison Commander of Rouxuan, Grand Director of the Inner and Outer Three Courts, and granted the title Marquis of Changjin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhen was Garrison Commander of Rouxuan and Grand Director of the Inner and Outer Three Courts, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Changjin.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈幽州刺史，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made Inspector of Youzhou, with the posthumous title Jian.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously appointed Inspector of Youzhou, with the posthumous title Jian.

sentences.zh: 康生少驍武，彎弓十石，矢異常箭，為當時所服。

translations.literal: Kangsheng in youth was fierce and martial; he could draw a bow of ten piculs and his arrows were unlike ordinary arrows—he was admired by his age.
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng in youth was fierce and martial; he could draw a bow rated at ten piculs and used extraordinary arrows, and men of his time admired him.

sentences.zh: 太和初，蠕蠕頻寇，康生為前驅軍主，壯氣有聞，由是為宗子隊主。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe the Rouran raided frequently; Kangsheng was vanguard army commander and his bold spirit was heard of, whereupon he became chief of the imperial clansmen's guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taihe era the Rouran raided frequently; Kangsheng served as vanguard army commander, and his bold spirit became well known, whereupon he was made chief of the imperial clansmen's guard.

sentences.zh: 從駕征鐘離，駕旋濟淮，五將未度，齊將據渚斷津路。

translations.literal: He followed the imperial carriage in the campaign against Zhongli; when the carriage turned back and crossed the Huai, the five generals had not yet crossed and Qi generals held the islet and cut the ford road.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the imperial carriage on the campaign against Zhongli. When the emperor turned back to cross the Huai, five generals had not yet crossed, and Qi forces held the mid-river islet and blocked the ford.

sentences.zh: 孝文募破中渚賊者，以為直閣將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen recruited one who could break the mid-islet rebels and made him a Direct Gate General.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen sought someone who could break the rebels on the mid-river islet and promised the post of Direct Gate General.

sentences.zh: 康生應募，縛筏積柴，因風放火，燒其船艦，依煙直過，飛刀亂斫，投河溺死者甚眾。

translations.literal: Kangsheng answered the call, bound rafts and piled firewood, took advantage of the wind to set fire, burned their ships, passed straight through in the smoke, hacked wildly with flying knives, and very many who fell into the river drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng answered the call, bound rafts and piled firewood, set fire with the wind, burned the enemy ships, charged straight through the smoke, hacked with thrown knives, and a great many men drowned in the river.

sentences.zh: 乃假康生直閣將軍。

translations.literal: He was then given Kangsheng the acting post of Direct Gate General.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed acting Direct Gate General.

sentences.zh: 後以勳除太子三校、西台直後。

translations.literal: Later for his merit he was made one of the Crown Prince's three guards and Attendant Behind the Western Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for his merit, he was made one of the Crown Prince's three guards and Attendant Behind the Western Terrace.

sentences.zh: 吐京胡反，自號辛支王，康生為軍主，從章武王彬討之。

translations.literal: The Hu of Tujing rebelled and styled themselves King Xinzhi; Kangsheng was army commander and followed the Prince of Zhangwu, Bin, to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu of Tujing rebelled and styled their leader King Xinzhi; Kangsheng served as army commander and followed the Prince of Zhangwu, Bin, against them.

sentences.zh: 分為五軍，四軍俱敗，康生軍獨全。

translations.literal: They were divided into five armies; four armies were all defeated and only Kangsheng's army remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: The force was divided into five armies; four were defeated, and only Kangsheng's army remained intact.

sentences.zh: 率精騎一千追胡至車突穀，詐為墜馬，胡皆謂死，爭欲取之。

translations.literal: He led a thousand crack horsemen in pursuit of the Hu to Chetu Valley, feigned falling from his horse, and the Hu all thought him dead and competed to take him.
translations.idiomatic: He led a thousand crack horsemen in pursuit to Chetu Valley, feigned a fall from his horse, and the Hu all thought him dead and rushed to seize him.

sentences.zh: 康生騰騎奮矛，殺傷數十人，射殺辛支。

translations.literal: Kangsheng leaped on his horse and thrust with his spear, killing and wounding several tens of men and shooting Xinzhi dead.
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng vaulted back into the saddle and thrust with his spear, killing or wounding several dozen men and shooting Xinzhi dead.

sentences.zh: 齊置義陽，招誘邊人，康生復為統軍，從王肅討之。

translations.literal: Qi established Yiyang to entice border people; Kangsheng again was commander-in-chief and followed Wang Su to campaign against it.
translations.idiomatic: Qi established Yiyang to entice border people; Kangsheng again served as commander-in-chief and followed Wang Su against it.

sentences.zh: 齊將張伏護自升樓城樓，言辭不遜。

translations.literal: The Qi general Zhang Fuhu ascended the tower of Shenglou city and his words were insolent.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi general Zhang Fuhu stood on the tower of Shenglou city and spoke insolently.
