sentences.zh: 肅令康生射之，望樓射窗，扉開即入，應箭而斃。

translations.literal: Su ordered Kangsheng to shoot him; he aimed at the tower window from afar, the door opened and the arrow entered, and Fuhu fell dead to the arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Su ordered Kangsheng to shoot him; aiming at the tower window from afar, he sent an arrow through as the door opened, and Fuhu fell dead.

sentences.zh: 彼人見箭，皆以為狂弩。

translations.literal: Those men, seeing the arrow, all thought it a mad crossbow.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders, seeing the arrow, all thought it must have come from a monstrous crossbow.

sentences.zh: 齊將裴叔業率眾圍渦陽，欲解義陽之急，詔遣高聰、元衍等援之，並敗退。

translations.literal: The Qi general Pei Shuye led masses to besiege Woyang to relieve the urgency at Yiyang; an edict sent Gao Cong, Yuan Yan, and others to aid it, and all were defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi general Pei Shuye led a large force to besiege Woyang and relieve Yiyang; the court sent Gao Cong, Yuan Yan, and others to aid the city, but all were defeated and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝乃遣康生馳往，一戰大破之。

translations.literal: The emperor then sent Kangsheng at full speed; in one battle he inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent Kangsheng at full speed, and in a single battle he won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 及壽春來降，遣康生領羽林千人，給龍廄馬兩匹，馳赴之。

translations.literal: When Shouchun came over in surrender, Kangsheng was sent leading a thousand Guards of the Feathered Forest, given two imperial stable horses, and hurried there.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouchun surrendered, Kangsheng was sent with a thousand Guards of the Feathered Forest and two imperial stable horses to hurry there.

sentences.zh: 破走其將桓和、陳伯之。

translations.literal: He routed and drove off their generals Huan He and Chen Bozhi.
translations.idiomatic: He routed and drove off the enemy generals Huan He and Chen Bozhi.

sentences.zh: 以功除征虜將軍，封安武縣男。

translations.literal: For his merit he was made General Who Punishes the Barbarians and enfeoffed as Baron of Anwu.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was appointed General Who Punishes the Barbarians and enfeoffed as Baron of Anwu.

sentences.zh: 出為南青州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Inspector of Southern Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Inspector of Southern Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 後梁鬱州遣軍主徐濟寇邊，康生破禽之。

translations.literal: Later Liang's Yuzhou sent the army commander Xu Ji to raid the border; Kangsheng defeated and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liang's Yuzhou sent the army commander Xu Ji to raid the border; Kangsheng defeated and captured him.

sentences.zh: 時梁聞康生能引強弓，故特作大弓兩張，長八尺，把中圍尺有二寸，箭粗殆如今之長笛，送與康生。

translations.literal: At that time Liang had heard that Kangsheng could draw a powerful bow, so they specially made two large bows eight chi long, with a grip circumference of one chi two inches in the middle, and arrows as thick as a long flute of today, and sent them to Kangsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liang had heard that Kangsheng could draw a powerful bow, so they specially made two large bows eight chi long, with a grip a foot and two inches around, and arrows as thick as a modern long flute, and sent them to him.

sentences.zh: 康生便集文武，用之平射，猶有餘力。

translations.literal: Kangsheng immediately gathered civil and military officers, used them in level shooting, and still had strength to spare.
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng immediately gathered his civil and military officers, drew the bows in level shooting, and still had strength to spare.

sentences.zh: 觀者以為絕倫。

translations.literal: The onlookers thought it unmatched in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers judged the feat unmatched in their time.

sentences.zh: 弓即表送，置之武庫。

translations.literal: The bows were then submitted by memorial and placed in the armory.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the bows to the throne and they were placed in the armory.

sentences.zh: 後梁遣都督臨川王蕭宏勒甲十萬規寇徐州，詔授康生武衛將軍，一戰敗之。

translations.literal: Later Liang sent the commander the Prince of Linchuan, Xiao Hong, to muster a hundred thousand armored men planning to raid Xuzhou; an edict made Kangsheng Martial Guard General, and in one battle he defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liang sent the commander, Prince of Linchuan Xiao Hong, to muster a hundred thousand armored men against Xuzhou; an edict appointed Kangsheng Martial Guard General, and he defeated them in a single battle.

sentences.zh: 還京，召見宴會，賞帛千匹，賜驊騮禦胡馬一匹。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital he was summoned to a banquet and rewarded with a thousand bolts of silk and one imperial chestnut horse of the Hu breed.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to the capital he was summoned to a banquet, rewarded with a thousand bolts of silk, and given one imperial chestnut horse of the Hu breed.

sentences.zh: 出為華州刺史，頗有聲績。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Inspector of Huazhou and had considerable reputation and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Inspector of Huazhou and earned a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 轉涇州刺史，以輒用官炭瓦，為御史所劾，削除官爵。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inspector of Jingzhou; for arbitrarily using official charcoal and tiles he was impeached by the censor and stripped of office and title.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Inspector of Jingzhou; for arbitrarily using government charcoal and tiles he was impeached by the censor and stripped of office and title.

sentences.zh: 尋復之。

translations.literal: Soon his titles were restored.
translations.idiomatic: His titles were soon restored.

sentences.zh: 梁直閣將軍徐玄明戍鬱州，殺其刺史張稷，以城內附，詔康生迎接；

translations.literal: The Liang Direct Gate General Xu Xuanming garrisoned Yuzhou, killed its inspector Zhang Ji, and submitted the city within; an edict ordered Kangsheng to go welcome him;
translations.idiomatic: The Liang Direct Gate General Xu Xuanming garrisoned Yuzhou, killed the inspector Zhang Ji, and surrendered the city; an edict ordered Kangsheng to go welcome him;

sentences.zh: 賜細禦銀纏槊一張，並棗柰果。

translations.literal: he was granted one fine imperial silver-wrapped spear and jujubes and pears.
translations.idiomatic: he was granted one fine imperial silver-wrapped spear, together with jujubes and pears.

sentences.zh: 面敕曰：「果者果如朕心，棗者早遂朕意。

translations.literal: In a face-to-face edict it was said, "Fruit—fruit like my heart; jujube—early fulfillment of my intent.
translations.idiomatic: In a face-to-face edict the emperor said, "Fruit—fruit like my heart; jujube—may my intent soon be fulfilled."

sentences.zh: 」未發間，郁州刺史復叛。

translations.literal: " Before he set out, the inspector of Yuzhou rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: " Before he set out, the inspector of Yuzhou rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 及大舉征蜀，假康生安西將軍，邪趣綿竹。

translations.literal: When a great campaign was launched against Shu, Kangsheng was given the acting post of General Who Pacifies the West and sent by a side route toward Mianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: When a great campaign was launched against Shu, Kangsheng was appointed acting General Who Pacifies the West and sent by a side route toward Mianzhu.

sentences.zh: 至隴右，宣武崩，班師。

translations.literal: When he reached Longyou, Emperor Xuanwu died and the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Longyou, Emperor Xuanwu died and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後除相州刺史，在州以天旱令人鞭石季龍畫像，復就西門豹祠祈雨，不獲，令吏取豹舌。

translations.literal: Later he was made Inspector of Xiangzhou; in the province, because of drought, he had men whip the portrait of Shi Jilong and again went to the shrine of Ximen Bao to pray for rain; when he did not obtain it he ordered an official to take Bao's tongue.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Inspector of Xiangzhou. During a drought in the province he had men whip a portrait of Shi Jilong and went to the shrine of Ximen Bao to pray for rain; when rain did not come he ordered an official to cut out Bao's tongue.

sentences.zh: 未幾，二兒暴喪，身亦遇疾，巫以為季龍、豹之祟。

translations.literal: Before long his two sons died suddenly and he himself fell ill; shamans said it was the harm of Jilong and Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his two sons died suddenly and he himself fell ill; shamans said it was the vengeance of Jilong and Bao.

sentences.zh: 徵拜光祿勳，領右衛將軍，與元叉同謀廢靈太后。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, concurrently General of the Right Guard, and with Yuan Cha plotted to depose Empress Dowager Ling.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and General of the Right Guard, and with Yuan Cha plotted to depose Empress Dowager Ling.

sentences.zh: 遷河南尹，仍右衛、領左右。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Governor of Henan, still holding Right Guard and directing the Left and Right.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Governor of Henan while retaining the Right Guard and directing the Left and Right guards.

sentences.zh: 與子難娶左衛將軍侯剛女，即元叉妹夫也。

translations.literal: He and his son Nan married the daughter of the General of the Left Guard Hou Gang—who was Yuan Cha's brother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: He and his son Nan married the daughter of the General of the Left Guard Hou Gang, who was Yuan Cha's brother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 叉以其通姻，深相委託，三人多宿禁內，或迭出入。

translations.literal: Cha because of this marriage tie deeply entrusted them; the three men often lodged within the forbidden precinct or went in and out in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the marriage tie Cha deeply entrusted them; the three men often lodged within the forbidden precinct or went in and out in rotation.

sentences.zh: 叉以康生子難為千牛備身。

translations.literal: Cha made Kangsheng's son Nan a Thousand-Ox Guard in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Cha made Kangsheng's son Nan a Thousand-Ox Guard in attendance.

sentences.zh: 康生性粗武，言氣高下。

translations.literal: Kangsheng by nature was rough and martial; his words and tone rose and fell.
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng was rough and martial by nature, and his words and tone rose and fell abruptly.

sentences.zh: 叉稍憚之，見於顏色，康生亦微懼不安。

translations.literal: Cha gradually feared him, which showed in his expression, and Kangsheng also felt slight fear and unease.
translations.idiomatic: Cha gradually came to fear him, which showed in his expression, and Kangsheng also felt uneasy.

sentences.zh: 正光二年二月，明帝朝靈太后于西林園。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Zhengguang, Emperor Ming paid court to Empress Dowager Ling in Xilin Garden.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the second year of Zhengguang, Emperor Ming paid court to Empress Dowager Ling in Xilin Garden.

sentences.zh: 文武侍坐，酒酣迭舞。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials sat in attendance; when the wine was deep they danced in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials sat in attendance; when the wine had gone deep they danced in turn.

sentences.zh: 次至康生，乃為力士舞，及於折旋。

translations.literal: When it came to Kangsheng, he then performed a strongman's dance, even to spinning turns.
translations.idiomatic: When Kangsheng's turn came, he performed a strongman's dance, even to spinning turns.

sentences.zh: 每顧視太后，舉手蹈足，嗔目頷首，為殺縛之勢。

translations.literal: Each time he looked back at the empress dowager he raised hands and stamped feet, glared and nodded his head, making the gesture of binding for killing.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he looked back at the empress dowager he raised his hands and stamped his feet, glared and nodded, miming the gesture of binding someone for execution.

sentences.zh: 太后解其意而不敢言。

translations.literal: The empress dowager understood his intent but did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager understood his intent but did not dare speak.

sentences.zh: 日暮，太后欲攜帝宿宣光殿。

translations.literal: At dusk the empress dowager wished to take the emperor to lodge in Xuanguang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk the empress dowager wished to take the emperor to lodge in Xuanguang Hall.

sentences.zh: 侯剛曰：「至尊已朝訖，嬪御在南，何勞留宿？

translations.literal: Hou Gang said, "The Son of Heaven has already finished his audience; the consorts are in the south—why trouble to lodge overnight?
translations.idiomatic: Hou Gang said, "The Son of Heaven has already finished his audience; the consorts are in the south—why trouble to lodge overnight?"

sentences.zh: 」康生曰：「至尊陛下兒，隨陛下將東西，更復訪問誰！

translations.literal: " Kangsheng said, "The Son of Heaven is Your Majesty's son; he follows Your Majesty wherever you go—whom else would you consult!
translations.idiomatic: " Kangsheng said, "The Son of Heaven is Your Majesty's son; he follows Your Majesty wherever you go—whom else would you consult?"

sentences.zh: 」群臣莫敢應。

translations.literal: " None of the officials dared answer.
translations.idiomatic: " None of the officials dared answer.

sentences.zh: 靈太后自起援帝臂，下堂而去；

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling herself rose to support the emperor's arm and went down from the hall;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling herself rose, took the emperor's arm, and went down from the hall;

sentences.zh: 康生大呼唱萬歲於後，近侍皆唱萬歲。

translations.literal: Kangsheng shouted "Long live!" from behind and the attendants near all shouted "Long live!"
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng shouted "Long live the emperor!" from behind, and the attendants nearby all shouted "Long live!"

sentences.zh: 明帝引前入閣，左右競相排，閣不得閉。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming was led forward into the inner gate; those left and right pushed against one another in competition and the gate could not be closed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming was led forward into the inner gate; attendants jostled one another in the crush and the gate could not be closed.

sentences.zh: 康生奪其子難千牛刀，斫直後元思輔，乃得定。

translations.literal: Kangsheng seized his son Nan's Thousand-Ox saber, hacked the Attendant Behind Yuan Sifu, and only then was it settled.
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng seized his son Nan's Thousand-Ox saber, struck down the Attendant Behind Yuan Sifu, and only then was order restored.

sentences.zh: 明帝既上殿，康生時有酒勢，將出處分；

translations.literal: After Emperor Ming had ascended the hall, Kangsheng, with the momentum of wine, was about to go out to give orders;
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Ming had ascended the hall, Kangsheng, still flushed with wine, was about to go out to give orders;

sentences.zh: 遂為叉所執，鎖于門下。

translations.literal: he was then seized by Cha and locked in the Gate Office.
translations.idiomatic: he was then seized by Cha and locked in the Gate Office.

sentences.zh: 至曉，叉不出，令侍中、黃門、僕射、尚書等十餘人就康生所，訊其事。

translations.literal: By dawn Cha did not come out and ordered more than ten Attendants-in-Chief, Yellow Gate officials, Vice Directors, and Directors of the Masters of Writing to go to Kangsheng's place and examine the matter.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn Cha had not emerged and ordered more than ten Attendants-in-Chief, Yellow Gate officials, Vice Directors, and Directors of the Masters of Writing to go to Kangsheng and examine the matter.

sentences.zh: 處康生斬刑，難處絞刑。

translations.literal: Kangsheng was sentenced to decapitation and Nan to strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng was sentenced to decapitation and Nan to strangulation.

sentences.zh: 叉與剛並在內矯詔決之。

translations.literal: Cha and Gang were both inside and forged an edict to decide it.
translations.idiomatic: Cha and Gang were both inside and forged an edict to decide the sentences.

sentences.zh: 康生如奏，難恕死從流。

translations.literal: Kangsheng as memorialized; Nan's death was pardoned and commuted to exile.
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng was executed as sentenced; Nan's death was pardoned and commuted to exile.

sentences.zh: 難哭拜辭父。

translations.literal: Nan wept and bowed in farewell to his father.
translations.idiomatic: Nan wept and bowed in farewell to his father.

sentences.zh: 康生忻子免死，慷慨了不悲泣。

translations.literal: Kangsheng, glad his son was spared death, was high-spirited and not sorrowful at all.
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng, glad his son had been spared death, was high-spirited and showed no grief at all.

sentences.zh: 語其子云：「我不反，死，汝何為哭也？

translations.literal: He said to his son, "I did not rebel; I die—why do you weep?
translations.idiomatic: He said to his son, "I did not rebel. I am to die—why do you weep?"

sentences.zh: 」有司驅逼，奔走赴市，時已昏暗，行刑人注刀數下，不死；

translations.literal: " The authorities drove and pressed him; he ran to the market. It was already dark; the executioner stabbed the blade several times and he did not die;
translations.idiomatic: " The authorities drove him onward; he ran to the execution ground. Night had already fallen; the executioner stabbed several times and still he did not die;

sentences.zh: 於地刻截。

translations.literal: On the ground they carved and cut him apart.
translations.idiomatic: On the ground they hacked him apart.

sentences.zh: 咸言稟叉意旨，過至苦痛。

translations.literal: All said it followed Cha's intent, going beyond to extreme agony.
translations.idiomatic: All agreed that the executioners had acted on Cha's orders, prolonging his agony beyond what the law required.

sentences.zh: 嘗食典禦奚混與康生同執刀入內，亦就市絞刑。

translations.literal: Once Palace Provision Master Xi Hun, together with Kangsheng wielding knives inside, likewise received strangulation at the market.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion Palace Provision Master Xi Hun had entered with Kangsheng, both with knives in hand; he too was taken to the market and strangled.

sentences.zh: 康生久為將，及臨州，多所殺戮。

translations.literal: Kangsheng had long served as a general; once he took up a provincial command, he killed many.
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng had been a general for many years; once he assumed provincial command, he slaughtered people on a large scale.

sentences.zh: 而乃信向佛道，每舍居宅立寺塔，凡曆四州，皆有建置。

translations.literal: Yet he believed in the Buddha-dharma; at each residence he established temples and pagodas—over four provinces in all, he built everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was a devout Buddhist; wherever he lived he erected temples and pagodas, and in every one of the four provinces he governed he left such monuments behind.

sentences.zh: 死時年五十四。

translations.literal: He died at the age of fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 子難年十八，以侯剛婿，得停百日，竟徙安州。

translations.literal: His son Nan, eighteen years old, as Hou Gang's son-in-law, was granted a hundred days' reprieve and was ultimately exiled to Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Nan, eighteen, was Hou Gang's son-in-law; he was granted a hundred-day reprieve before being exiled to Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 後尚書盧同為行台，叉令殺之。

translations.literal: Later, when Lu Tong of the Masters of Writing served as Mobile Directorate, Cha ordered Nan killed.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Lu Tong of the Masters of Writing served as Mobile Directorate, Cha ordered Nan executed.

sentences.zh: 康生於南山立佛圖三層，先死，忽夢崩壞。

translations.literal: Kangsheng had built a three-story Buddhist pagoda on the southern mountain; before his death he suddenly dreamed it collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng had erected a three-story Buddhist pagoda on the southern mountain; shortly before his death he dreamed that it had collapsed.

sentences.zh: 沙門有為解云：「檀越當不吉利，無人供養佛圖，故崩耳。

translations.literal: A monk named Youwei interpreted, saying, "Patron, you will meet ill fortune; no one will make offerings to the pagoda, hence its collapse.
translations.idiomatic: A monk named Youwei offered an interpretation: "Your merit will not end well, Patron—no one will maintain the pagoda, and so it falls in your dream."

sentences.zh: 」康生稱然，竟及於禍。

translations.literal: " Kangsheng agreed; in the end calamity befell him.
translations.idiomatic: Kangsheng agreed with this reading—and calamity did indeed befall him.

sentences.zh: 靈太后反政，贈都督冀瀛滄三州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、司空、冀州刺史，諡曰武貞，又追封壽張縣侯。

translations.literal: When Empress Ling resumed power, he was posthumously appointed Commander-in-Chief over the armies of Ji, Ying, and Cang provinces, Grand General of Fast Cavalry, Minister of Works, and Inspector of Jizhou, with posthumous title Wuzhen, and later enfeoffed retroactively as Marquis of Shouzhang.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Ling regained power, Kangsheng was posthumously appointed commander over the military affairs of Ji, Ying, and Cang provinces, made Grand General of Fast Cavalry, Minister of Works, and Inspector of Jizhou, given the posthumous name Wuzhen, and later retroactively enfeoffed as Marquis of Shouzhang.

sentences.zh: 子剛襲。

translations.literal: His son Gang inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gang inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 楊大眼，武都氐難當之孫也。

translations.literal: Yang Dayan was a grandson of the Di chieftain Nan Dang of Wudu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Dayan was a grandson of Nan Dang, the Di chieftain of Wudu.

sentences.zh: 少驍捷，跳走如飛。

translations.literal: From youth he was fierce and nimble; running and leaping, he moved like flight.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he was fierce and agile; when he ran and leaped he seemed almost to fly.

sentences.zh: 然庶孽，不為宗親顧待，不免饑寒。

translations.literal: However, as a bastard son, he received no care from clan kin and could not escape hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: But he was born of a concubine, and the clan gave him little support, so he knew hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 太和中，起家奉朝請。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he began his career as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era he entered service as a Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 時將南伐，尚書李沖典選征官，大眼往求焉，沖弗許。

translations.literal: When a southern campaign was about to be launched, Minister Li Chong was in charge of selecting campaign officers; Dayan went to ask but Chong refused.
translations.idiomatic: When a southern campaign was being mounted, Li Chong of the Masters of Writing was selecting officers for it; Dayan applied but Chong turned him down.

sentences.zh: 大眼曰：「尚書不見知，聽下官出一技。

translations.literal: Dayan said, "Since the Minister does not recognize my worth, allow this lowly officer to show one skill.
translations.idiomatic: Dayan said, "Since the Minister does not recognize my worth, allow this lowly officer to show one skill."

sentences.zh: 」便出長繩三丈許，系髻而走，繩直如矢，馬馳不及。

translations.literal: " He produced a rope some three zhang long, tied it to his topknot and ran; the rope stretched straight as an arrow, and a galloping horse could not keep pace.
translations.idiomatic: He took out a rope nearly three zhang long, tied it to his topknot, and ran; the rope stayed straight as an arrow while no horse at full gallop could catch him.

sentences.zh: 見者無不驚歎。

translations.literal: All who saw it were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone who watched was astonished.

sentences.zh: 沖因曰：「千載以來，未有逸材若此者也。

translations.literal: Chong thereupon said, "For a thousand years there has been no outstanding talent like this.
translations.idiomatic: Chong thereupon said, "For a thousand years there has been no outstanding talent like this."

sentences.zh: 」遂用為軍主。

translations.literal: " He was then appointed Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed an army commander.

sentences.zh: 大眼顧謂同寮曰：「吾之今日，所謂蛟龍得水之秋。

translations.literal: Dayan turned to his colleagues and said, "Today for me is what they call the season when the flood dragon meets water.
translations.idiomatic: Dayan turned to his colleagues and said, "Today for me is what they call the season when the flood dragon meets water."

sentences.zh: 自此一舉，不復與諸君齊列矣。

translations.literal: From this one chance I shall no longer rank among you all together.
translations.idiomatic: From this one chance I shall no longer rank among you all together.

sentences.zh: 」未幾，遷統軍，從車駕征宛、葉、穰、鄧、九江、鐘離之間，所經戰陣，莫不勇冠六軍。

translations.literal: " Before long he was promoted to Army Commander-in-Chief and followed the imperial carriage in campaigns among Wan, Ye, Rang, Deng, Jiujiang, and Zhongli; in every battle he fought, his bravery topped the Six Armies.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Army Commander-in-Chief and followed the imperial carriage in campaigns among Wan, Ye, Rang, Deng, Jiujiang, and Zhongli; in every battle he fought, his bravery topped the Six Armies.

sentences.zh: 宣武初，裴叔業以壽春內附，大眼與奚康生等率眾先入，以功封安成縣子。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Xuanwu's reign, Pei Shuye brought Shouchun over to Wei; Dayan and Xi Kangsheng and others led troops in first and for merit were enfeoffed as Viscount of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xuanwu's reign, Pei Shuye surrendered Shouchun to Wei; Dayan and Xi Kangsheng and others were first into the city and were enfeoffed as Viscount of Ancheng for their service.

sentences.zh: 除直閣將軍，出為東荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Direct Palace Gate General and went out as Inspector of Eastern Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Direct Palace Gate General and went out as Inspector of Eastern Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時蠻酋樊秀安等反，詔大眼為別將，隸都督李崇討平之，大眼功尤多。

translations.literal: When the barbarian chieftains Fan Xiuan and others rebelled, an edict made Dayan a detached commander under Area Commander Li Chong to suppress them; Dayan's merit was especially great.
translations.idiomatic: When the barbarian chieftains Fan Xiuan and others rebelled, an edict made Dayan a detached commander under Area Commander Li Chong to suppress them; Dayan's merit was especially great.

sentences.zh: 妻潘氏，善騎射，自詣軍省大眼。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Pan was skilled at mounted archery and came on her own to join Dayan in camp.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Pan was skilled at mounted archery and came on her own to join Dayan in camp.

sentences.zh: 至攻戰遊獵之際，潘亦戎裝，齊鑣並驅。

translations.literal: When it came to attacking in battle and hunting, Pan also donned military garb and rode side by side with him.
translations.idiomatic: In battle and on the hunt alike, Lady Pan donned armor and rode at his side.

sentences.zh: 及至還營，同坐幕下，對諸寮佐，言笑自得。

translations.literal: When they returned to camp, they sat together beneath the tent awning before the staff officers, talking and laughing at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When they returned to camp, they sat together beneath the tent awning before the staff officers, talking and laughing at ease.

sentences.zh: 大眼時指謂諸人曰：「此潘將軍也。」

translations.literal: Dayan would point at her and tell everyone, "This is General Pan."
translations.idiomatic: Dayan would point at her and tell everyone, "This is General Pan."

sentences.zh: 梁武遣其將張惠紹總率眾軍，竊據宿豫。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang sent his general Zhang Huishao to lead the armies and seize Suzhou by stealth.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang sent his general Zhang Huishao to lead the armies and seize Suzhou by stealth.

sentences.zh: 又假大眼平東將軍為別將，與都督邢巒討破之。

translations.literal: Dayan was again given provisional rank as General Who Pacifies the East and made detached commander; with Area Commander Xing Luan he defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Dayan was again given provisional rank as General Who Pacifies the East and made detached commander; with Area Commander Xing Luan he defeated them.

sentences.zh: 遂與中山王英同圍鐘離。

translations.literal: He then joined Prince of Zhongshan Yuan Ying in besieging Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Prince of Zhongshan Yuan Ying in besieging Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 大眼軍城東，守淮橋東西道。

translations.literal: Dayan's army was east of the city, guarding the eastern and western approaches to the Huai Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Dayan's army was east of the city, guarding the eastern and western approaches to the Huai Bridge.

sentences.zh: 屬水泛長，大眼所綰統軍劉神符、公孫祉兩軍夜中爭橋奔退，大眼不能禁，相尋而走。

translations.literal: As floods rose, the Army Commanders Liu Shenfu and Gongsun Zhi under Dayan's command fought at night to cross the bridge and fled; Dayan could not restrain them and they withdrew one after another.
translations.idiomatic: As floods rose, the Army Commanders Liu Shenfu and Gongsun Zhi under Dayan's command fought at night to cross the bridge and fled; Dayan could not restrain them and they withdrew one after another.

sentences.zh: 坐徙營州為兵。

translations.literal: For this he was punished by exile to Yingzhou as a common soldier.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was punished by exile to Yingzhou as a common soldier.

sentences.zh: 永平中，追其前勳，起為試守中山內史。

translations.literal: In the Yongping era, recalling his earlier merit, he was recalled to serve as provisional Administrator of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongping era, recalling his earlier merit, he was recalled to serve as provisional Administrator of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 時高肇征蜀，宣武慮梁人侵軼，乃征大眼為太尉長史、持節、假平南將軍、東征別將，隸都督元遙，遏禦淮、肥。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhao campaigned in Shu, Emperor Xuanwu feared Liang incursions and summoned Dayan as Chief Administrator to the Grand Commandant, with staff of authority, provisional rank as General Who Pacifies the South, and Eastern Campaign detached commander under Area Commander Yuan Yao to block Liang along the Huai and Fei.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhao campaigned in Shu, Emperor Xuanwu feared Liang incursions and summoned Dayan as Chief Administrator to the Grand Commandant, with staff of authority, provisional rank as General Who Pacifies the South, and Eastern Campaign detached commander under Area Commander Yuan Yao to block Liang along the Huai and Fei.

sentences.zh: 大眼至京師，時人思其雄勇，喜於更用，台省門巷，觀者如市。

translations.literal: When Dayan arrived at the capital, people missed his heroic bravery and rejoiced at his reappointment; the alleys outside offices were packed like a market.
translations.idiomatic: When Dayan arrived at the capital, people missed his heroic bravery and rejoiced at his reappointment; the alleys outside offices were packed like a market.

sentences.zh: 後梁將康絢於浮山遏淮，規浸壽春。

translations.literal: Later Liang general Kang Xuan dammed the Huai at Fushan, planning to flood Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Later Liang general Kang Xuan dammed the Huai at Fushan, planning to flood Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 明帝加大眼光祿大夫，率諸軍鎮荊山，復其封邑。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaoming promoted Dayan to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, had him lead the armies to garrison Jingshan, and restored his fief.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaoming promoted Dayan to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, had him lead the armies to garrison Jingshan, and restored his fief.

sentences.zh: 後與蕭寶夤俱征淮堰，不能克，遂於堰上流鑿渠決水而還。

translations.literal: Later he joined Xiao Baoyin in campaigning against the Huai dam but could not capture it; they then cut channels upstream to release the water and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined Xiao Baoyin in campaigning against the Huai dam but could not capture it; they then cut channels upstream to release the water and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 加平東將軍。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 大眼撫循士卒，呼為兒子，及見傷痍，為之流泣。

translations.literal: Dayan comforted his soldiers, calling them his sons; when he saw the wounded he wept for them.
translations.idiomatic: Dayan comforted his soldiers, calling them his sons; when he saw the wounded he wept for them.

sentences.zh: 自為將帥，恆身先兵士，當其鋒者，莫不摧拉。

translations.literal: As a commander he always led from the front; whoever met his charge was shattered.
translations.idiomatic: As a commander he always led from the front; whoever met his charge was shattered.

sentences.zh: 南賊所遣督將，皆懷畏懼。

translations.literal: Every supervising general the southern enemy sent feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Every supervising general the southern enemy sent feared him.

sentences.zh: 時傳言淮、泗、荊、沔之間童兒啼者，恐之云「楊大眼至」，無不即止。

translations.literal: It was said that among children crying between the Huai, Si, Jing, and Mian rivers, whoever frightened them by saying "Yang Dayan is coming" would at once be silenced.
translations.idiomatic: It was said that among children crying between the Huai, Si, Jing, and Mian rivers, whoever frightened them by saying "Yang Dayan is coming" would at once be silenced.

sentences.zh: 王肅弟康之初歸國也，謂大眼曰：「在南聞君之名，以為眼如車輪。

translations.literal: When Wang Su's younger brother Kang, newly returned to the north, said to Dayan, "In the south I heard your name and imagined your eyes were like carriage wheels.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Su's younger brother Kang, newly returned to the north, said to Dayan, "In the south I heard your name and imagined your eyes were like carriage wheels."

sentences.zh: 及見，乃不異於人。

translations.literal: Now that I see you, they are no different from anyone else's.
translations.idiomatic: Now that I see you, they are no different from anyone else's.

sentences.zh: 」大眼曰：「旗鼓相望，瞋眸奮發，足使君目不能視，何必大如車輪。

translations.literal: " Dayan said, "When banners and drums face each other and I glare and rage, that alone will keep your eyes from seeing—why need they be as large as carriage wheels?
translations.idiomatic: Dayan said, "When banners and drums face each other and I glare and rage, that alone will keep your eyes from seeing—why need they be as large as carriage wheels?"

sentences.zh: 」當世推其驍果，以為關、張弗之過也。

translations.literal: " His contemporaries praised his fierce valor, deeming him the equal of Guan Yu and Zhang Fei.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries praised his fierce valor, deeming him the equal of Guan Yu and Zhang Fei.

sentences.zh: 然征淮堰之役，喜怒無常，捶撻過度，軍士頗憾焉。

translations.literal: Yet during the Huai dam campaign his moods swung wildly; he beat men excessively and the troops resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet during the Huai dam campaign his moods swung wildly; he beat men excessively and the troops resented it.

sentences.zh: 識者以為性移所致。

translations.literal: Those who understood such things attributed it to a change in his temperament.
translations.idiomatic: Those who understood such things attributed it to a change in his temperament.

sentences.zh: 又為荊州刺史，常縛槁為人，衣以青布而射之。

translations.literal: Again serving as Inspector of Jingzhou, he often bound straw into human shapes, dressed them in blue cloth, and shot them.
translations.idiomatic: Again serving as Inspector of Jingzhou, he often bound straw into human shapes, dressed them in blue cloth, and shot them.

sentences.zh: 召諸蠻渠，指示之曰：「卿等若作賊，吾政如此相殺也。

translations.literal: He summoned the barbarian chieftains, pointed at the figures, and said, "If you turn to banditry, this is how I will kill you.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the barbarian chieftains, pointed at the figures, and said, "If you turn to banditry, this is how I will kill you."

sentences.zh: 」又北淯郡嘗有虎害，大眼搏而獲之，斬其頭縣於穰市。

translations.literal: " In Beiyu commandery there had once been a tiger plague; Dayan wrestled and captured it, cut off its head, and hung it in the market at Rang.
translations.idiomatic: In Beiyu commandery there had once been a tiger plague; Dayan wrestled and captured it, cut off its head, and hung it in the market at Rang.

sentences.zh: 自是荊蠻相謂曰：「楊公惡人，常作我蠻形以射之。

translations.literal: From then on the barbarians of Jing said to one another, "That villain Yang Dayan constantly makes figures of us and shoots them.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the barbarians of Jing said to one another, "That villain Yang Dayan constantly makes figures of us and shoots them."

sentences.zh: 又深山之虎，尚所不免。

translations.literal: Even the mountain tigers deep in the hills could not escape him.
translations.idiomatic: Even the mountain tigers deep in the hills could not escape him.

sentences.zh: 」遂不敢復為寇盜。

translations.literal: " After that they dared not raid again.
translations.idiomatic: After that they dared not raid again.

sentences.zh: 在州二年，卒。

translations.literal: After two years in the province, he died.
translations.idiomatic: After two years in the province, he died.

sentences.zh: 大眼雖不學，恆遣人讀書而坐聽之，悉皆記識。

translations.literal: Though Dayan was unlettered, he always had someone read aloud while he listened seated, and remembered it all.
translations.idiomatic: Though Dayan was unlettered, he always had someone read aloud while he listened seated, and remembered it all.

sentences.zh: 令作露布，皆口授之，而竟不多識字也。

translations.literal: When he had bulletins of victory drafted, he dictated them all by mouth, yet in the end he knew few written characters.
translations.idiomatic: When he had bulletins of victory drafted, he dictated them all by mouth, yet in the end he knew few written characters.

sentences.zh: 有三子，長甑生，次領軍，次征南，皆潘氏所生，咸有父風。

translations.literal: He had three sons: the eldest Zengsheng, the next Lingjun, and the youngest Zhengnan—all born of Lady Pan and all bearing their father's martial bearing.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: the eldest Zengsheng, the next Lingjun, and the youngest Zhengnan—all born of Lady Pan and all bearing their father's martial bearing.

sentences.zh: 初，大眼徙營州，潘在洛陽，頗有失行。

translations.literal: When Dayan was first exiled to Yingzhou, Pan remained in Luoyang and behaved rather improperly.
translations.idiomatic: When Dayan was first exiled to Yingzhou, Pan remained in Luoyang and behaved rather improperly.

sentences.zh: 及為中山，大眼側生女夫趙延寶告之於大眼。

translations.literal: When he became Administrator of Zhongshan, Dayan's son-in-law by a concubine daughter, Zhao Yanbao, reported this to Dayan.
translations.idiomatic: When he became Administrator of Zhongshan, Dayan's son-in-law by a concubine daughter, Zhao Yanbao, reported this to Dayan.

sentences.zh: 大眼怒，幽潘而殺之。

translations.literal: Dayan in anger imprisoned Pan and killed her.
translations.idiomatic: Dayan in anger imprisoned Pan and killed her.

sentences.zh: 後娶繼室元氏。

translations.literal: He later married Lady Yuan as his successor wife.
translations.idiomatic: He later married Lady Yuan as his successor wife.

sentences.zh: 大眼之死也，甑生等問印綬所在。

translations.literal: When Dayan died, Zengsheng and the others asked where the seals and cords were.
translations.idiomatic: When Dayan died, Zengsheng and the others asked where the seals and cords were.

sentences.zh: 時元始懷孕，自指其腹謂甑生等曰：「開國當我兒襲之，汝等婢子，勿有所望。

translations.literal: Lady Yuan was pregnant; she pointed to her belly and told Zengsheng and the others, "The founding fief will pass to my son; you servant-born whelps should hope for nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yuan was pregnant; she pointed to her belly and told Zengsheng and the others, "The founding fief will pass to my son; you servant-born whelps should hope for nothing."

sentences.zh: 」甑生等深以為恨。

translations.literal: " Zengsheng and the others deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Zengsheng and the others deeply resented this.

sentences.zh: 及大眼喪將還京，出於城東七里，營車而宿。

translations.literal: When Dayan's funeral train was to return to the capital, they camped seven li east of the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Dayan's funeral train was to return to the capital, they camped seven li east of the city.

sentences.zh: 夜二更，甑生等開大眼棺，延寶怪而問焉，征南射殺之。

translations.literal: At the second watch of the night Zengsheng and the others opened Dayan's coffin; Yanbao wondered and questioned them, and Zhengnan shot him dead.
translations.idiomatic: At the second watch of the night Zengsheng and the others opened Dayan's coffin; Yanbao wondered and questioned them, and Zhengnan shot him dead.

sentences.zh: 元怖，走入水，征南又彎弓將射之。

translations.literal: Lady Yuan in terror fled into the water; Zhengnan again bent his bow to shoot her.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yuan in terror fled into the water; Zhengnan again bent his bow to shoot her.

sentences.zh: 甑生曰：「天下豈有害母之人。

translations.literal: Zengsheng said, "Under heaven can there be a man who would harm his mother?
translations.idiomatic: Zengsheng said, "Under heaven can there be a man who would harm his mother?"

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " He stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: He stopped him.

sentences.zh: 遂取大眼屍，令人馬上抱之，左右扶挾以叛。

translations.literal: They then took Dayan's corpse, had men hold it on horseback, supported on either side, and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: They then took Dayan's corpse, had men hold it on horseback, supported on either side, and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 荊人畏甑生等驍武，不敢苦追，遂奔梁。

translations.literal: The people of Jing feared the fierce courage of Zengsheng and the others and did not press the pursuit; they fled to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Jing feared the fierce courage of Zengsheng and the others and did not press the pursuit; they fled to Liang.

sentences.zh: 崔延伯，博陵人也。

translations.literal: Cui Yanbo was a man of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yanbo was from Boling.

sentences.zh: 祖壽，于彭城陷入江南。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shou was captured at Pengcheng and fell into the lands south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shou was captured at Pengcheng and fell into the lands south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 延伯少以武壯聞，仕齊為緣淮遊軍，帶濠口戍主。

translations.literal: Yanbo was known from youth for martial prowess; he served Qi as a mobile army along the Huai and concurrently as garrison commander at Haokou.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo was known from youth for martial prowess; he served Qi as a mobile army along the Huai and concurrently as garrison commander at Haokou.

sentences.zh: 太和中入魏。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he entered Wei service.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era he entered Wei service.

sentences.zh: 常為統帥，膽氣絕人，兼有謀略，積勞稍進。

translations.literal: He often served as commander-in-chief; his courage surpassed others and he also had strategy; through accumulated service he gradually advanced.
translations.idiomatic: He often served as commander-in-chief; his courage surpassed others and he also had strategy; through accumulated service he gradually advanced.

sentences.zh: 除征虜將軍、荊州刺史，賜爵定陵男。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Captures Barbarians and Inspector of Jingzhou, and enfeoffed as Baron of Dingling.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Captures Barbarians and Inspector of Jingzhou, and enfeoffed as Baron of Dingling.

sentences.zh: 荊州土險，蠻左為寇，每有聚結，延伯輒自討之，莫不摧殄。

translations.literal: Jingzhou's terrain was rugged and the barbarian tribes raided; whenever they gathered, Yanbo personally campaigned against them and destroyed them without fail.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou's terrain was rugged and the barbarian tribes raided; whenever they gathered, Yanbo personally campaigned against them and destroyed them without fail.

sentences.zh: 由是穰土帖然，無敢為患。

translations.literal: Thereby the lands around Rang were pacified and none dared cause trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby the lands around Rang were pacified and none dared cause trouble.

sentences.zh: 永平中，轉幽州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Yongping era he was transferred to Inspector of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongping era he was transferred to Inspector of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 梁遣左遊擊將軍趙祖悅率眾偷據硤石，詔延伯為別將，與都督崔亮討之。

translations.literal: Liang sent Left Mobile Strike General Zhao Zuyue to lead troops and seize Xiashi by stealth; an edict made Yanbo detached commander to join Area Commander Cui Liang in suppressing him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang sent Left Mobile Strike General Zhao Zuyue to lead troops and seize Xiashi by stealth; an edict made Yanbo detached commander to join Area Commander Cui Liang in suppressing him.

sentences.zh: 亮令延伯守下蔡。

translations.literal: Cui Liang ordered Yanbo to hold Xiaocai.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Liang ordered Yanbo to hold Xiaocai.

sentences.zh: 延伯與別將伊瓫生挾淮為營。

translations.literal: Yanbo and detached commander Yi Mousheng set camp straddling the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo and detached commander Yi Mousheng set camp straddling the Huai.

sentences.zh: 延伯遂取車輪，去輞，削銳其輻，兩兩接對，揉竹為糸亙，貫連相屬，並十餘道。

translations.literal: Yanbo then took cart wheels, removed the rims, sharpened the spokes, paired them spoke to spoke, twisted bamboo into cords to link them in succession—more than ten such lines in all.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo then took cart wheels, removed the rims, sharpened the spokes, paired them spoke to spoke, twisted bamboo into cords to link them in succession—more than ten such lines in all.

sentences.zh: 橫水為橋，兩頭施大鹿盧，出沒任情，不可燒斫，既斷祖悅走路，又令舟舸不通。

translations.literal: He laid them across the water as a bridge, with large capstans at both ends; it could be raised or lowered at will, could neither be burned nor cut—it cut off Zuyue's escape and blocked boats as well.
translations.idiomatic: He laid them across the water as a bridge, with large capstans at both ends; it could be raised or lowered at will, could neither be burned nor cut—it cut off Zuyue's escape and blocked boats as well.

sentences.zh: 由是梁軍不能赴救，祖悅合軍咸見俘虜。

translations.literal: Thus Liang armies could not come to the rescue, and all of Zuyue's combined forces were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Liang armies could not come to the rescue, and all of Zuyue's combined forces were captured.

sentences.zh: 于軍拜征南將軍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the field he was appointed General Who Conquers the South and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the field he was appointed General Who Conquers the South and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 延伯與楊大眼等至自淮陽，靈太后幸西林園引見，謂曰：「卿等志尚雄猛，皆國之名將。

translations.literal: When Yanbo and Yang Dayan and others returned from Huaiyang, Empress Ling visited the Western Forest Garden to receive them and said, "Your ambitions are fierce and bold—you are all famed generals of the state.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanbo and Yang Dayan and others returned from Huaiyang, Empress Ling visited the Western Forest Garden to receive them and said, "Your ambitions are fierce and bold—you are all famed generals of the state."

sentences.zh: 比平硤石、公私慶快，此乃卿等之功也。

translations.literal: The recent pacification of Xiashi has brought joy to court and people alike—this is your achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The recent pacification of Xiashi has brought joy to court and people alike—this is your achievement.

sentences.zh: 但淮堰仍在，宜須預謀，故引卿等，親共量算，各出一圖，以為後計。

translations.literal: But the Huai dam still stands and must be planned for; therefore I have summoned you to measure and calculate together, each offering a plan for what lies ahead.
translations.idiomatic: But the Huai dam still stands and must be planned for; therefore I have summoned you to measure and calculate together, each offering a plan for what lies ahead.

sentences.zh: 」大眼對曰：「臣輒謂水陸二道一時俱下，往無不克。

translations.literal: " Dayan replied, "Your servant holds that if land and water forces advance together at once, none can fail to take it.
translations.idiomatic: Dayan replied, "Your servant holds that if land and water forces advance together at once, none can fail to take it."

sentences.zh: 」延伯曰：「既對聖顏，答旨宜實。

translations.literal: " Yanbo said, "Facing the imperial presence, my answer must be honest.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo said, "Facing the imperial presence, my answer must be honest."

sentences.zh: 水南水北，各有溝瀆，陸地之計，如何可前。

translations.literal: South of the water and north of the water each have ditches and canals—how can a land plan advance?
translations.idiomatic: South of the water and north of the water each have ditches and canals—how can a land plan advance?

sentences.zh: 愚臣短見，願聖心思水兵之勤，若給復一年，專習水戰，脫有不虞，召便可用。

translations.literal: Your foolish servant's short view is that Your Majesty should consider the labor of water forces; if granted one year of exemption and devoted training in naval warfare, should anything unexpected arise, they could be summoned and used at once.
translations.idiomatic: Your foolish servant's short view is that Your Majesty should consider the labor of water forces; if granted one year of exemption and devoted training in naval warfare, should anything unexpected arise, they could be summoned and used at once.

sentences.zh: 」靈太后曰：「卿之所言，深是宜要，當敕如請。

translations.literal: " Empress Ling said, "What you say is very much to the point; it shall be ordered as you request.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Ling said, "What you say is very much to the point; it shall be ordered as you request."

sentences.zh: 」二年，除并州刺史。

translations.literal: " In the second year he was appointed Inspector of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed Inspector of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 在州貪污，聞於遠近。

translations.literal: In the province he was corrupt; word spread far and near.
translations.idiomatic: In the province he was corrupt; word spread far and near.

sentences.zh: 還為金紫光祿大夫，出為鎮南將軍，行岐州刺史，假征西將軍。

translations.literal: He returned as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Tassel, went out as General Who Guards the South, acting Inspector of Qizhou, and provisional General Who Conquers the West.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Tassel, went out as General Who Guards the South, acting Inspector of Qizhou, and provisional General Who Conquers the West.

sentences.zh: 賜驊騮馬一匹。

translations.literal: He was granted one Ferghana horse.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted one Ferghana horse.

sentences.zh: 正光五年秋，以往在揚州，建淮橋之勳，封當利縣男，改封新豐子。

translations.literal: In autumn of the fifth year of Zhengguang, for his earlier service at Yangzhou building the Huai bridge, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Dangli and later changed to Viscount of Xinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of the fifth year of Zhengguang, for his earlier service at Yangzhou building the Huai bridge, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Dangli and later changed to Viscount of Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 時莫折念生兄天生下隴東寇，征西將軍元志為天生所禽，賊眾甚盛，進屯黑水。

translations.literal: At that time Moqi Niansheng's elder brother Tiansheng came down from Long eastward to raid; General Who Conquers the West Yuan Zhi was captured by Tiansheng; the rebel host was very strong and advanced to encamp at Heishui.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Moqi Niansheng's elder brother Tiansheng came down from Long eastward to raid; General Who Conquers the West Yuan Zhi was captured by Tiansheng; the rebel host was very strong and advanced to encamp at Heishui.

sentences.zh: 詔延伯為使持節、征西將軍、西道都督。

translations.literal: An edict made Yanbo Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Conquers the West, and Western Route Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Yanbo Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Conquers the West, and Western Route Area Commander.

sentences.zh: 行台蕭寶夤與延伯結壘馬嵬，南北相去百餘步。

translations.literal: Mobile Directorate Xiao Baoyin and Yanbo built camps at Maqi, north and south some hundred-odd paces apart.
translations.idiomatic: Mobile Directorate Xiao Baoyin and Yanbo built camps at Maqi, north and south some hundred-odd paces apart.

sentences.zh: 延伯曰：「今當仰為明公參賊勇怯。

translations.literal: Yanbo said, "Now I shall on your behalf gauge the enemy's courage and cowardice.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo said, "Now I shall on your behalf gauge the enemy's courage and cowardice."

sentences.zh: 」延伯選精兵數千，下度黑水，列陣而進，以向賊營。

translations.literal: " Yanbo selected several thousand elite troops, descended and crossed the Heishui, formed ranks and advanced toward the rebel camp.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo selected several thousand elite troops, descended and crossed the Heishui, formed ranks and advanced toward the rebel camp.

sentences.zh: 寶夤率騎于水東尋原西北，以示後繼。

translations.literal: Baoyin led cavalry along the east bank following the high ground northwest to show that reinforcements followed.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin led cavalry along the east bank following the high ground northwest to show that reinforcements followed.

sentences.zh: 于時賊眾大盛，水西一里，營營連接。

translations.literal: At that time the rebel forces were very strong; west of the water for a li, camp after camp connected.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the rebel forces were very strong; west of the water for a li, camp after camp connected.

sentences.zh: 延伯徑至賊壘，揚威脅之，徐而還退。

translations.literal: Yanbo went straight to the rebel ramparts, displayed might and threatened them, then slowly withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo went straight to the rebel ramparts, displayed might and threatened them, then slowly withdrew.

sentences.zh: 賊以延伯眾少，開營競追，眾過十倍，臨水逼蹙。

translations.literal: The rebels, seeing Yanbo's few troops, opened camp and raced in pursuit; their numbers exceeded his tenfold and they pressed him to the water's edge.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels, seeing Yanbo's few troops, opened camp and raced in pursuit; their numbers exceeded his tenfold and they pressed him to the water's edge.

sentences.zh: 寶夤親觀之，懼有虧損。

translations.literal: Baoyin watched in person and feared losses.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin watched in person and feared losses.

sentences.zh: 延伯不與其戰，身自殿后，抽眾東度，轉運如神。

translations.literal: Yanbo did not engage them; he personally brought up the rear, drew his troops eastward across the water, wheeling with godlike speed.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo did not engage them; he personally brought up the rear, drew his troops eastward across the water, wheeling with godlike speed.

sentences.zh: 須臾濟盡，徐乃自度。

translations.literal: In a moment all had crossed; only then did he leisurely cross himself.
translations.idiomatic: In a moment all had crossed; only then did he leisurely cross himself.

sentences.zh: 賊徒奪氣，相率還營。

translations.literal: The rebels lost their fighting spirit and withdrew to camp in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels lost their fighting spirit and withdrew to camp in succession.

sentences.zh: 寶夤大悅，謂宮屬曰：「崔公，古之關、張也，今年何患不制賊。

translations.literal: Baoyin was greatly pleased and told his staff, "Lord Cui is a Guan Yu or Zhang Fei of old—what worry is there this year of not subduing the rebels?
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin was greatly pleased and told his staff, "Lord Cui is a Guan Yu or Zhang Fei of old—what worry is there this year of not subduing the rebels?"

sentences.zh: 」延伯馳見寶夤曰：「此賊非老奴敵，公但坐看。

translations.literal: " Yanbo galloped to see Baoyin and said, "These rebels are no match for this old servant—you need only sit and watch.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo galloped to see Baoyin and said, "These rebels are no match for this old servant—you need only sit and watch."

sentences.zh: 」後日，延伯勒眾而出，寶夤為後拒。

translations.literal: " The next day Yanbo marshaled his troops and went out; Baoyin served as rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yanbo marshaled his troops and went out; Baoyin served as rear guard.

sentences.zh: 天生悉眾來戰，延伯身先士卒，陷其前鋒。

translations.literal: Tiansheng came with his full force; Yanbo led from the front and broke their vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Tiansheng came with his full force; Yanbo led from the front and broke their vanguard.

sentences.zh: 於是驍銳競進，大破之，俘斬十餘萬，追奔及於小隴。

translations.literal: Thereupon the fierce elite pressed forward, routed them utterly, captured and killed more than a hundred thousand, and pursued the rout to Xiao Long.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the fierce elite pressed forward, routed them utterly, captured and killed more than a hundred thousand, and pursued the rout to Xiao Long.

sentences.zh: 秦賊勁強，諸將所憚，初議遣將，咸雲非延伯無以定之，果能克敵。

translations.literal: The Qin rebels were powerful and the generals feared them; when first discussing whom to send, all said only Yanbo could settle it—and he indeed defeated the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin rebels were powerful and the generals feared them; when first discussing whom to send, all said only Yanbo could settle it—and he indeed defeated the enemy.

sentences.zh: 詔授左衛將軍，余如故。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Left Guard General; the rest unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him Left Guard General; the rest unchanged.

sentences.zh: 于時万俟醜奴、宿勤明達等寇掠涇州。

translations.literal: At that time Moqi Chounu, Suqin Mingda, and others raided Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Moqi Chounu, Suqin Mingda, and others raided Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是盧祖遷、伊瓫生數將，皆以元志前行之始，同時發雍，從六陌道將取高平。

translations.literal: Earlier Lu Zuqian, Yi Mousheng, and several generals, all at the start of Yuan Zhi's advance, had set out together from Yong along the Liumo road intending to take Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Lu Zuqian, Yi Mousheng, and several generals, all at the start of Yuan Zhi's advance, had set out together from Yong along the Liumo road intending to take Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 志敗，仍停涇部。

translations.literal: When Zhi was defeated, they remained in the Jing region.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhi was defeated, they remained in the Jing region.

sentences.zh: 延伯既破秦賊，乃與寶夤率眾會于安定。

translations.literal: After Yanbo had broken the Qin rebels, he and Baoyin led their hosts to meet at Anding.
translations.idiomatic: After Yanbo had broken the Qin rebels, he and Baoyin led their hosts to meet at Anding.

sentences.zh: 甲卒十二萬，鐵馬八千匹，軍威甚盛。

translations.literal: Armored soldiers numbered a hundred and twenty thousand, iron horses eight thousand—military might was very great.
translations.idiomatic: Armored soldiers numbered a hundred and twenty thousand, iron horses eight thousand—military might was very great.

sentences.zh: 時醜奴置營涇州西北七十里當原城。

translations.literal: At that time Chounu had encamped seventy li northwest of Jingzhou at Dangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chounu had encamped seventy li northwest of Jingzhou at Dangyuan.

sentences.zh: 時或輕騎暫來挑戰，大兵未交，便示奔北。

translations.literal: Sometimes light cavalry would come briefly to challenge; before the main forces met, they would feign flight.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes light cavalry would come briefly to challenge; before the main forces met, they would feign flight.

sentences.zh: 延伯矜功負勝，遂唱議先驅。

translations.literal: Yanbo, proud of his merit and confident from victory, then proposed taking the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo, proud of his merit and confident from victory, then proposed taking the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 伐木別造大排，內為鎖柱，教習強兵；

translations.literal: He felled trees and specially built great palisades with locking pillars inside, drilling strong troops;
translations.idiomatic: He felled trees and specially built great palisades with locking pillars inside, drilling strong troops;

sentences.zh: 負而趨走，號為排城。

translations.literal: they carried them while running—called 'Palisade Fortresses.'
translations.idiomatic: they carried them while running—called 'Palisade Fortresses.'

sentences.zh: 戰士在外，輜重居中，自涇州緣原北上。

translations.literal: Warriors on the outside, baggage in the center—they marched north along the plateau from Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Warriors on the outside, baggage in the center—they marched north along the plateau from Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 眾軍將出討賊。

translations.literal: The assembled armies were about to march out against the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The assembled armies were about to march out against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 未戰之間，有賊數百騎詐持文書，雲是降簿，乞緩師。

translations.literal: Before battle, several hundred rebel horsemen fraudulently held documents claiming they were registers of surrender, begging a halt to the advance.
translations.idiomatic: Before battle, several hundred rebel horsemen fraudulently held documents claiming they were registers of surrender, begging a halt to the advance.

sentences.zh: 寶夤、延伯謂其事實，逡巡未鬥。

translations.literal: Baoyin and Yanbo took it for real and hesitated without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin and Yanbo took it for real and hesitated without fighting.

sentences.zh: 俄而宿勤明達率眾自東北而至，乞降之賊從西競下，諸軍前後受敵。

translations.literal: Soon Suqin Mingda led his host from the northeast; the 'surrendering' rebels charged down from the west—the armies were attacked front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Suqin Mingda led his host from the northeast; the 'surrendering' rebels charged down from the west—the armies were attacked front and rear.

sentences.zh: 延伯上馬突陣，賊勢摧挫，便爾逐北，徑造其營。

translations.literal: Yanbo mounted and charged the formation; rebel momentum was broken and he at once pursued north straight to their camp.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo mounted and charged the formation; rebel momentum was broken and he at once pursued north straight to their camp.

sentences.zh: 賊本輕騎，延伯軍兼步卒，兵力疲怠，賊乃乘間得入排城。

translations.literal: The rebels were originally light cavalry; Yanbo's army included foot soldiers whose strength was spent—the rebels seized the opening and entered the palisade fortresses.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were originally light cavalry; Yanbo's army included foot soldiers whose strength was spent—the rebels seized the opening and entered the palisade fortresses.

sentences.zh: 延伯軍大敗，死傷者將有二萬。

translations.literal: Yanbo's army was routed; dead and wounded approached twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo's army was routed; dead and wounded approached twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 寶夤斂軍退保涇州。

translations.literal: Baoyin gathered his troops and fell back to defend Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin gathered his troops and fell back to defend Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 延伯修繕器械，購募驍勇，復從涇州西進，去賊彭阬穀柵七里結營。

translations.literal: Yanbo repaired weapons, recruited fierce men, and again advanced west from Jingzhou, encamping seven li from the rebels' Pengkeng Valley palisade.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo repaired weapons, recruited fierce men, and again advanced west from Jingzhou, encamping seven li from the rebels' Pengkeng Valley palisade.

sentences.zh: 延伯恥前挫辱，不報寶夤，獨出襲賊，大破之。

translations.literal: Ashamed of his earlier defeat, Yanbo did not report to Baoyin but went out alone to raid the rebels and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed of his earlier defeat, Yanbo did not report to Baoyin but went out alone to raid the rebels and routed them.

sentences.zh: 俄頃間平其數柵。

translations.literal: In a brief span he levelled several palisades.
translations.idiomatic: In a brief span he levelled several palisades.

sentences.zh: 賊皆逃迸。

translations.literal: The rebels all fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels all fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 見兵人采掠，散亂不整，還來衝突，遂大奔敗。

translations.literal: Seeing the troops looting in disorder, the rebels turned and charged again, and Yanbo's men were routed utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the troops looting in disorder, the rebels turned and charged again, and Yanbo's men were routed utterly.

sentences.zh: 延伯中流矢，為賊所害，士卒死者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Yanbo was struck by a stray arrow and killed by the rebels; more than ten thousand soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo was struck by a stray arrow and killed by the rebels; more than ten thousand soldiers died.

sentences.zh: 延伯善將撫，能得眾心，與康生、大眼為諸將之冠。

translations.literal: Yanbo was skilled at commanding and comforting men and could win the hearts of the host; with Kangsheng and Dayan he stood at the head of the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo was skilled at commanding and comforting men and could win the hearts of the host; with Kangsheng and Dayan he stood at the head of the generals.

sentences.zh: 延伯末路，功名尤重。

translations.literal: In his final years Yanbo's fame and merit were especially great.
translations.idiomatic: In his final years Yanbo's fame and merit were especially great.

sentences.zh: 時大寇未平而延伯死，朝野歎懼焉。

translations.literal: When the great rebels were not yet pacified and Yanbo died, court and people alike lamented and feared.
translations.idiomatic: When the great rebels were not yet pacified and Yanbo died, court and people alike lamented and feared.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、定州刺史，諡曰武烈。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Three Analogues, and Inspector of Dingzhou, with posthumous title Wulie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Three Analogues, and Inspector of Dingzhou, with posthumous title Wulie.

sentences.zh: 李叔仁，隴西人也。

translations.literal: Li Shuren was a man of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shuren was from Longxi.

sentences.zh: 驍健有武力，前後數從征討，以功賜爵獲城鄉男。

translations.literal: Fierce and strong with martial prowess, he followed campaigns time and again and for merit was enfeoffed as Baron of Huocheng Township.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce and strong with martial prowess, he followed campaigns time and again and for merit was enfeoffed as Baron of Huocheng Township.

sentences.zh: 梁豫州刺史王超宗內侵，叔仁時為兼統軍，隸揚州刺史薛真度。

translations.literal: When Liang Inspector of Yuzhou Wang Chaozong invaded inward, Shuren was then concurrent Army Commander-in-Chief under Yangzhou Inspector Xue Zhendu.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Inspector of Yuzhou Wang Chaozong invaded inward, Shuren was then concurrent Army Commander-in-Chief under Yangzhou Inspector Xue Zhendu.

sentences.zh: 真度遣叔仁討超宗，大破之。

translations.literal: Zhendu sent Shuren against Chaozong and routed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhendu sent Shuren against Chaozong and routed him.

sentences.zh: 以功累遷洛州刺史，假撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted in succession to Inspector of Luozhou and given provisional rank as General Who Pacifies the Armies.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was promoted in succession to Inspector of Luozhou and given provisional rank as General Who Pacifies the Armies.

sentences.zh: 後以軍功封陳郡公，又除光祿大夫、朔州刺史。

translations.literal: Later for military merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Chen commandery and appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Inspector of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later for military merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Chen commandery and appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Inspector of Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 齊州廣川人劉執、清河太守邵懷，聚眾反，自署大行台。

translations.literal: Liu Zhi of Guangchuan in Qizhou and Qinghe Administrator Shao Huai gathered followers and rebelled, proclaiming themselves a Mobile Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhi of Guangchuan in Qizhou and Qinghe Administrator Shao Huai gathered followers and rebelled, proclaiming themselves a Mobile Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 詔叔仁為都督，討平之。

translations.literal: An edict made Shuren Area Commander to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Shuren Area Commander to suppress and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 除鎮西將軍、金紫光祿大夫，轉車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Guards the West and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Tassel, then transferred to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Three Analogues.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Guards the West and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Tassel, then transferred to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Three Analogues.

sentences.zh: 邢果反于青州，叔仁為大都督，出討於淮，失利而還。

translations.literal: When Xing Guo rebelled in Qingzhou, Shuren was made Grand Area Commander, marched out against him at the Huai, suffered defeat, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Xing Guo rebelled in Qingzhou, Shuren was made Grand Area Commander, marched out against him at the Huai, suffered defeat, and returned.

sentences.zh: 永安三年，坐事除名，尋復官爵。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yong'an he was stripped of rank for an offense; soon his title and office were restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yong'an he was stripped of rank for an offense; soon his title and office were restored.

sentences.zh: 節閔帝初，加散騎常侍、開府。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Jiemin's reign he was given the additional titles Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of an Area Command.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Jiemin's reign he was given the additional titles Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of an Area Command.

sentences.zh: 後除涼州刺史。

translations.literal: He was later appointed Inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 遣使密通款於東魏，事覺見殺。

translations.literal: He sent envoys secretly to communicate submission with Eastern Wei; when the matter was discovered he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys secretly to communicate submission with Eastern Wei; when the matter was discovered he was executed.

sentences.zh: 叔仁所用之槊，長大異于常槊，時人壯之。

translations.literal: The spear Shuren used was long and large, unlike ordinary spears; people of the time admired it.
translations.idiomatic: The spear Shuren used was long and large, unlike ordinary spears; people of the time admired it.

sentences.zh: 論曰：韓茂、皮豹子、封敕文、呂羅漢、孔伯恭之為將也，皆以沈勇篤實，仁厚扶眾，功成事立，不徒然矣。

translations.literal: Commentary: Han Mao, Pi Baozi, Feng Chiwen, Lu Luohan, and Kong Bogong as generals all relied on deep courage, solid truthfulness, and benevolent care for the host; their achievements and deeds stood—not in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Han Mao, Pi Baozi, Feng Chiwen, Lu Luohan, and Kong Bogong as generals all relied on deep courage, solid truthfulness, and benevolent care for the host; their achievements and deeds stood—not in vain.

sentences.zh: 與夫苟要一戰之利，僥倖暫勝之名，豈同年而語也。

translations.literal: Compared with those who grasp only the profit of one battle or the name of a lucky fleeting victory—how can they be spoken of in the same year?
translations.idiomatic: Compared with those who grasp only the profit of one battle or the name of a lucky fleeting victory—how can they be spoken of in the same breath?

sentences.zh: 田益宗蠻夷荒帥，翻然效款，終於懷金曳紫，不其美歟。

translations.literal: Tian Yizong, a barbarian chieftain of the wilderness, turned and offered allegiance, and in the end wore gold seals and purple cords—is this not fine?
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yizong, a barbarian chieftain of the wilderness, turned and offered allegiance, and in the end wore gold seals and purple cords—is this not fine?

sentences.zh: 孟表之致名位，不徒然也。

translations.literal: Meng Biao's attainment of fame and rank was not in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Biao's attainment of fame and rank was not in vain.

sentences.zh: 夫人主聞鞞鼓之響，則思將帥之臣，何則？

translations.literal: When a ruler hears the sound of drums and battle, he thinks of his generals—why is this?
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler hears the sound of drums and battle, he thinks of his generals—why is this?

sentences.zh: 夷難平暴，折沖禦侮，為國之所系也。

translations.literal: To pacify hardship and suppress violence, to break the enemy's charge and repel insult—the state depends on these things.
translations.idiomatic: To pacify hardship and suppress violence, to break the enemy's charge and repel insult—the state depends on these things.

sentences.zh: 奚康生等俱以熊虎之姿，奮征伐之氣，亦一時之驍猛，壯士之功名乎。

translations.literal: Xi Kangsheng and the others all possessed the bearing of tiger and bear, exerting the spirit of expedition—also for their time fierce and bold, the achievements and fame of warriors.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Kangsheng and the others all possessed the bearing of tiger and bear, exerting the spirit of expedition—also for their time fierce and bold, the achievements and fame of warriors.
